name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: This is most of what running for office actually looks like:
body:
There’s a behind-the-scenes picture in this email.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Take a look at this, Peter:
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261010_1_grwm.g1HQNv&refcode=em20261010-2374&t=1&akid=2374%2E299639%2E_Lz5zW)
**Somebody on my team dug up this photo from the campaign trail.**
That’s me in a public bathroom, probably off an exit on I-35, between one campaign stop and the next, getting ready to speak in front of thousands of people.
This is most of what running for office actually looks like — bathroom mirrors, gas station coffee, a Whataburger bag on the passenger seat, and a voice that’s about one more speech from giving out.
I wouldn’t trade a minute of it, Peter. Because a few minutes after photos like this one are taken, **I’m in a room full of people who drove a long way to be in community with us.**
People who stay after to share their stories with me. Teachers donating blood two or three times a week to make ends meet. A woman in Brownsville whose mother’s electric bill hit $600 in a single month.
They tell me these things, and then without hesitation, they ask me how they can help our campaign. That’s the part I’ll never get over: Our shared belief that Texas ought to belong to the people who live here.
I believe we’re closer to that Texas than we’ve been in a generation — but with 24 days left, we can’t afford to let up. There are a lot more rooms to get to and voters to reach before this thing is decided.
**[If you’re with us, will you chip in what you can today and help us stay on the road?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261010_1_grwm.g1HQNv&refcode=em20261010-2374&t=2&akid=2374%2E299639%2E_Lz5zW)**

Thank you, Peter.
– Gina Hinojosa

Pray as though it all depends on God and act as though it all depends on us. To put it simply, we cannot lose Arizona to Democrats in 2026. Without Arizona, roughly 70% of the statistical paths to the White House disappear. >> Whoever is the governor of Arizona will oversee the 2028 election. We need to win to secure the election. >> Arizona is the most consequential state in the presidential election. Lose it here, and 2028 gets a lot harder to win. >> Whoever wins the White House in 2028 runs the census. Whoever runs the census draws the lines for 2032. That's a decade of ground we don't get back. Here's how we win Arizona: We win by deploying real people, knocking on doors, building real relationships with real voters. It's having ballot chasers in the field every single day until Election Day. We've done it before. Our ballot chasers helped beat a Kamala-backed city councilwoman here in Arizona. They delivered a win in the Salt River Project race against a wall of environmental spending. And of course, it's how we delivered Arizona for Trump in 2028! This works. We've proven it works. Now we need to fund it at scale. Turning Point PAC is trying to raise $94,000 this week to put ballot chasers in the field across Arizona. This is bigger than one election
Three states are about to decide a lot more than 2026.

Fellow Patriot,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let me explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.

name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Dinner with some of America’s leading conservatives
body:
Come and have dinner with some of the leading conservatives in America. | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/msgala2026?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
Come and have dinner with some of the leading conservatives in America. On Thursday, October 22, Charles C.W. Cooke of National Review, Grover Norquist of Americans for Tax Reform and Speaker Jason White will join us at the Country Club of Jackson. I would very much like you to be there too. Last Saturday I wrote about how America is starting to notice Mississippi. How fourth graders here now out-read their peers in California and New York. How investment keeps arriving. How young people from the Northeast are heading south in their thousands. This is not happening by accident. It is happening because of decisions, made by people, in the face of stiff opposition. Many of those people will be in the room that evening. **A Celebration of Mississippi’s Success .....** Our annual gala runs from 7pm to 9pm. It is the one evening each year when Mississippi’s business leaders, legislators, philanthropists and supporters gather to take stock of how far our state has come, and where it goes next. This year’s line-up is, I think, the strongest we have ever put together.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/IZx3n3n9gIi?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)
---
_Click on the photo above to reserve your tickets!_
| **Who you will hear from .....** Speaker Jason White will be with us. When I told you that Mississippi is the first state to legislate to remove its income tax since Alaska in 1980, that was his legislation. Few people have done more to change the trajectory of our state. Grover Norquist, founder of Americans for Tax Reform, will join the discussion. For forty years Grover has argued that states could, and should, abolish the income tax. He was told it could never be done. Mississippi is now doing it. I suspect he will have something to say about that. And our keynote speaker is Charles C.W. Cooke of National Review. He is one of the sharpest conservative minds writing today, and one of the most entertaining. If you listen to “The Editors” podcast, you will know exactly what I mean. **Why this year matters .....** As I wrote last week, no one in the South is standing still. Arkansas, Alabama, Tennessee and others are racing to catch up, and in some areas they have already overtaken us. The gains we have made can be built on, or they can be squandered. This evening is about making sure it is the former. It is where the case for the next round of reform begins. Guests will enjoy dinner, a private VIP reception, and the chance to spend an evening with the people shaping Mississippi’s future. Every ticket supports our work to advance free markets, individual liberty and limited government across our state. **Reserve your place .....** Seats at the Country Club are finite, and once they are gone, they are gone.
---

Douglas Carswell

| BRAVE for Good Join me in reclaiming our children's hearts | | | | | Dear Patriot, If you haven’t heard about “See You at the Library Day” on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, please let me tell you why it’s so critical. Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian. She would fill your mind with classics like Pat the Bunny and The Little Engine That Could. And eventually you got old enough to roam by yourself and discover adventures like the Three Musketeers, Treasure Island and Charlotte’s Web. But today, all that has changed. Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, the president of the American Library Association (ALA) says libraries should be used to address ‘systemic racism’ and elevate ‘BIPOC and GLBTQR+ writers and voices.’ Radical librarians call Adventures of Huckleberry Finn and To Kill a Mockingbird “racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her “problematic’ Little House series. And they bring in men wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to children of all ages... A is for Activist. An ABC board book for “families who want their kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism, environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else that activists believe in and fight for.” Woke Baby. “For all the littlest progressives, waking up to seize a new day of justice and activism. Woke babies raise their fists in the air. Woke babies cry out for justice. Woke babies grow up to change the world.” Prince and Knight. The “premier queer-friendly fairy tale” about a prince who marries a knight instead of a princess. And The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish. A “family-friendly celebration of drag” that encourages children to “work it.” I wish I could tell you this was only happening in places like New York City and San Francisco...but that’s just not true. **[That’s why parents and grandparents across the country are rising up through See You At The Library Day.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjUsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA3KP8hRtbgf8nOiG5YvOrMhumnpDHkMzLRM9ASCCbrhbbuhU3gv_BETkySgODKqk0RvZG6nrfkg-fIAmA55ERmaMBOMff59gSNURjv0D)**
---
[](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjUsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA3KP8hRuqEZsUtu5Ps1Ynz7UJxOw6Z_0TjMyTA8w4WcWtZ8VC6RMBfINJn0cL5pr14c9R5Cj9u5jtJusvpSUBdN04fyT5JfwDB27Y0lH)
---
For decades, the ultra-liberal Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and George Soros’ Open Society have spent millions radicalizing the ALA. And as a result, a new generation of pink-haired, activist librarians have made it their mission to fill library shelves with anti-American, LGBTQ-friendly, and explicitly sexual content. Maybe you’ve noticed all the displays at your own library celebrating Pride Month or elevating ‘the environment’ to a type of religion. Or maybe you’ve noticed the “Teen Zone” which is really meant to be a “parent-free” zone. The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: Rick about a cross-dressing Grandpa, Melissa filled with graphic nudity, and Darkstalker featuring gory violence and domestic abuse. But here’s what’s really alarming. We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.” That may be good for your family -- for now. But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of other children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values! I hope you see why I need your help today. Last year, committed conservatives just like you booked event rooms at 201 libraries in 46 states. On the same day, across America hundreds of “Story Hours” filled children’s hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God. Conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots stood together for a very simple mission -- to reject the Left’s radical ideas and reclaim childhood innocence in America’s libraries. **And this year, honoring America’s 250th birthday, my ambitious goal is to expand “See You at the Library Day” to reach 250,000 children.** [**The****date is October 3****rd****and a****nd before then, I need you!**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwMjUsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA3KP8hRvq07jTmbKsFcx04iZLAgkfp8vt42Fxk0Zyc1q3eaXK5cDTWR_krcS_mN4mZotPusIyQ3a_dKaOdsG9Mo7CItc4GqwwKRxxGMv) The response from parents, grandparents, and patriots who want to host “Story Hours” has been overwhelming. That’s a very good thing. **But****it’s****going to be a big undertaking and expensive to give these volunteers the resources they need to hold “Story Hours” for****250,000 children****by the 3****rd****.** Your sponsorship gift helps send a ‘Story Hour Kit’ to every parent, grandparent, and patriot who’s organizing a “See You at the Library” event. The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards, and other specialty items. **Your sponsorship gift is the only way we can fund our “Story Hours” for 250,000 children to counter the radical leftists who’ve taken control of our libraries.** We don’t have the millions behind us like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA. Knowing that, please consider a sponsorship gift of $125. That’s enough to sponsor one entire ‘Story Hour Kit’ yourself. Singlehandedly, you’ll be reaching 50 children with our wholesome, Godly, and patriotic message. Whatever you can give whether it’s $35, $125, or anything higher or lower please send in your sponsorship gift as soon as possible so we know how many libraries we have sponsored for this year’s “See You at the Library Day.”

clean_body: | | | | | | | | | | | "View in Browser" A Special Message from our Sponsor Please note that views expressed in this message do not necessarily reflect those of Free Speech Daily and do not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by Free Speech Daily . | BRAVE for Good Join me in reclaiming our children's hearts | | | | | Dear Patriot, If you haven’t heard about “See You at the Library Day” on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, please let me tell you why it’s so critical. Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian. She would fill your mind with classics like Pat the Bunny and The Little Engine That Could. And eventually you got old enough to roam by yourself and discover adventures like the Three Musketeers, Treasure Island and Charlotte’s Web. But today, all that has changed. Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, the president of the American Library Association (ALA) says libraries should be used to address ‘systemic racism’ and elevate ‘BIPOC and GLBTQR+ writers and voices.’ Radical librarians call Adventures of Huckleberry Finn and To Kill a Mockingbird “racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her “problematic’ Little House series. And they bring in men wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to children of all ages... A is for Activist. An ABC board book for “families who want their kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism, environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else that activists believe in and fight for.” Woke Baby. “For all the littlest progressives, waking up to seize a new day of justice and activism. Woke babies raise their fists in the air. Woke babies cry out for justice. Woke babies grow up to change the world.” Prince and Knight. The “premier queer-friendly fairy tale” about a prince who marries a knight instead of a princess. And The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish. A “family-friendly celebration of drag” that encourages children to “work it.” I wish I could tell you this was only happening in places like New York City and San Francisco...but that’s just not true. For decades, the ultra-liberal Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and George Soros’ Open Society have spent millions radicalizing the ALA. And as a result, a new generation of pink-haired, activist librarians have made it their mission to fill library shelves with anti-American, LGBTQ-friendly, and explicitly sexual content. Maybe you’ve noticed all the displays at your own library celebrating Pride Month or elevating ‘the environment’ to a type of religion. Or maybe you’ve noticed the “Teen Zone” which is really meant to be a “parent-free” zone. The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: Rick about a cross-dressing Grandpa, Melissa filled with graphic nudity, and Darkstalker featuring gory violence and domestic abuse. But here’s what’s really alarming. We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.” That may be good for your family -- for now. But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of other children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values! I hope you see why I need your help today. Last year, committed conservatives just like you booked event rooms at 201 libraries in 46 states. On the same day, across America hundreds of “Story Hours” filled children’s hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God. Conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots stood together for a very simple mission -- to reject the Left’s radical ideas and reclaim childhood innocence in America’s libraries. And this year, honoring America’s 250th birthday, my ambitious goal is to expand “See You at the Library Day” to reach 250,000 children. The response from parents, grandparents, and patriots who want to host “Story Hours” has been overwhelming. That’s a very good thing. Butit’sgoing to be a big undertaking and expensive to give these volunteers the resources they need to hold “Story Hours” for250,000 childrenby the 3rd. Your sponsorship gift helps send a ‘Story Hour Kit’ to every parent, grandparent, and patriot who’s organizing a “See You at the Library” event. The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards, and other specialty items. Your sponsorship gift is the only way we can fund our “Story Hours” for 250,000 children to counter the radical leftists who’ve taken control of our libraries. We don’t have the millions behind us like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA. Knowing that, please consider a sponsorship gift of $125. That’s enough to sponsor one entire ‘Story Hour Kit’ yourself. Singlehandedly, you’ll be reaching 50 children with our wholesome, Godly, and patriotic message. Whatever you can give whether it’s $35, $125, or anything higher or lower please send in your sponsorship gift as soon as possible so we know how many libraries we have sponsored for this year’s “See You at the Library Day.” | | | Thank you! God Bless You and God Bless America, Dr. Trent Talbot | | | | BRAVE FOR GOOD is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. Your gift is tax-deductible to the full extent allowed by law. | | | | Peter, How do you successfully execute a 45-million-acre corporate land grab? **Step one:** You take an executive who spent his career lobbying to chop down national forests. **Step two:** You appoint him as the Chief of the U.S. Forest Service. Step three: You wait for him to open the floodgates. **That is exactly what is happening right now in Washington.** Tom Schultz is the first-ever Forest Service Chief who didn't actually come from within the agency. Before this, he was the president of a timber trade association. Now, he is using his government authority to completely kill the 25-year-old "roadless rule," stripping protections from 45 million acres of untouched wilderness so his former employers can bulldoze roads and clear-cut the backcountry. The politicians rubber-stamping this heist are looking the American public in the eye and claiming they need to build logging roads into pristine habitats to "prevent wildfires." It is complete garbage. [**This is a 45-million-acre heist happening in broad daylight. Will you pitch in $10 today to our rapid-response war chest so we can expose this corruption?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/cJ4ZhxvfEZrbcpTG1pYzbg~~/AAUS1hA~/gICB6g64aUMg0K33LisJOS4ry3dMuYJ7vCwM1PIzerk4-L7-QoFlTMnLwSigFhxxIW0HcUDLjbZ3WTt4DzSohRJ5Q6aPxXelEnsQWaPR1SCYCVNH72Hqr1KcO1T8t0-yAP6nf1z0U2C1V_XLoOYjaOxmoOF2AHR1m77n89-G8kP8BpGf7dBA8WSkbF11ml4l6RqLPLhaoutTGEkZPphMR6uxP4Oc-MDW1K8IuqHdawZC69CJ9ZgB_hKEvK0d6aOT) The Forest Service's _own data_ shows that wildfires are nearly three times as likely to start near roads because they bring in human ignition sources. They aren't trying to stop forest fires—they are using the threat of fires as a human shield for the timber lobby. And the lumber executives know it. They are literally bragging on corporate earnings calls, telling their Wall Street investors, "We know the new Forest Service chief." Schultz and the politicians enabling him think they can quietly liquidate the last remaining old-growth forests in America without facing any consequences. They expect you to be too exhausted by the news cycle to put up a fight. We are going to ensure that every hunter, angler, hiker, and voter knows exactly who allowed a timber lobbyist to sell off our national heritage. [**Will you chip in $10, $25, or $50 today to help us fund the backlash and hold them accountable at the ballot box?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/yIiYbT4VNzl3C8vizn5PBw~~/AAUS1hA~/b5M3AxQbXCNnRFLquzCu291ajqzfXP-Rm7Td2_kUNLsxZmSMk3co2qPIuRN_vvITOq222RlyPdillVtFIyLB9qpLNvctozu8cKC2dNelD6JfhRVAimeQulIzJfOYTSaAvusgpg2Joz300uq3pA_OlsPEM76ZUQpkT1uPUCo-NFhtosdGJoPqpJzYbfcxJNAR_Z-hYKZDQKa9excmVA_ZoWrOiVlApPRVvHZaj1nG4ABinX5o33jjdHeGI5GY3Ug3) **[**DONATE »** ](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/yIiYbT4VNzl3C8vizn5PBw~~/AAUS1hA~/b5M3AxQbXCNnRFLquzCu291ajqzfXP-Rm7Td2_kUNLsxZmSMk3co2qPIuRN_vvITOq222RlyPdillVtFIyLB9qpLNvctozu8cKC2dNelD6JfhRVAimeQulIzJfOYTSaAvusgpg2Joz300uq3pA_OlsPEM76ZUQpkT1uPUCo-NFhtosdGJoPqpJzYbfcxJNAR_Z-hYKZDQKa9excmVA_ZoWrOiVlApPRVvHZaj1nG4ABinX5o33jjdHeGI5GY3Ug3) ** Thank you. Hi team,
Sometimes when I'm out on the campaign trail or hosting a town hall, I'll think to myself:

**These are the people Dan Meuser is so afraid of.**
They don't bite, Dan. I promise!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7c5c9be9-cae0-4740-b814-6a5a1c58cab6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Dan has spent his whole tenure in Congress hiding from the people he represents - from farmers, seniors, small business owners, health care workers, families, and everyone else he's screwed over.
**He 's terrified to be held accountable. So he spends all of his time going to fancy fundraisers, sucking up to his corporate donors, or being anywhere else but our part of PA.**
On Monday, Dan's going to be a special guest at a meet-and-greet _in another district._ He'll go talk to someone else's constituents, but never his own.
**The one place Dan can 't hide from the people is in the voting booth.**
If we reach every single voter possible in the next 24 days, we can finally hold Dan accountable and give our district real representation in Congress.

subject: The New York Times: Greg Abbott trailing
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
The New York Times last polled our race 3 months ago and found us down 7. This poll has swung 10 points since then.

| | |
---
Friend, look at this:
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5897?refcode=jtk1548-bu-nd&t=1&akid=13086%2E400544%2EWbtw2C)
In June, _The_ _New York Times_ /Siena poll had me trailing Greg Abbott by 7 points, 51% to 44%.
**Now, that same poll has me ahead, 49% to 46%.**
That's a 10-point swing in three months, from one of the most respected pollsters in the country. It's not a fluke, either. This is the third poll showing us ahead of Abbott, and it's the most recent one, taken after weeks of Abbott's attack ads flooding Texas airwaves. [**Split $5 right now between Deb Haaland's campaign and my campaign to help us turn this polling lead into a win.**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5898?refcode=jtk1548-bu-nd&t=2&akid=13086%2E400544%2EWbtw2C)
_The_ _New York Times_ also ran a major story on the state of play in Texas. Read this:
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5897?refcode=jtk1548-bu-nd&t=3&akid=13086%2E400544%2EWbtw2C)
**Ten-to-one. Abbott has thrown everything he has at this race, and he still can't put it away.**
Wendy Davis put it this way in the same article: "People have vastly underestimated Gina. Dollar for dollar, she's running the best statewide campaign we've ever seen."
That's what grassroots supporters like you have built $5 and $10 at a time. We haven't come close to matching Abbott's money, but every dollar has gone further than anyone thought it could. [**Will you split a contribution today between Deb Haaland's campaign and my campaign to help us keep our momentum going in the final stretch?**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5897?refcode=jtk1548-bu-nd&t=4&akid=13086%2E400544%2EWbtw2C)
The Times was also honest about what still stands in our way. Texas has 20 separate media markets, and national donors routinely pass the state over because reaching all of them is so expensive. And one in five Texas voters still doesn't know who I am.
Here's what the last three months have taught us: The more Texans get to know me, the more this race moves. **Every one of those voters is someone we can reach, but only if we have the resources to do it.** Abbott has raised more than $106 million in this race, and he's going to keep spending it in the final month to drag this race back his way.
We are 24 days from Election Day. The polls tell us this race can be won. What happens next depends on whether we have the financial resources to communicate our message to the voters who need to hear it.
[**Can you split $5 right now between Deb Haaland's campaign and my campaign to help us reach every voter in every corner of Texas and defeat Greg Abbott on Nov. 3?**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5898?refcode=jtk1548-bu-nd&t=5&akid=13086%2E400544%2EWbtw2C)

We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.

Jim Himes is polished, articulate, and comfortable in front of a television camera. He's good at it like an actor and could be nominated for an Oscar for his performances and sound bites criticizing President Trump, and exaggerating his impact in representing the people of Connecticut.
But Congress isn't Hollywood and the Congress Street Bridge in Bridgeport that he ran on fixing 18 years ago has become a park and a homeless encampment.
Congress is where laws are written, taxpayer dollars are spent, and decisions are made that affect our families, businesses, and communities.
**The question isn 't how good Jim Himes looks on television. It's what he's actually doing for Connecticut and as the saying goes - "Is he bringing home the bacon?" If I shook a Magic 8 ball the Survey says No.**
## So What Does the Record Show?
The website [YourRepRecord](https://substack.com/redirect/7a29eba6-e52e-494f-a770-c32e10e89051?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tracks congressional voting activity across 12 policy areas.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/22edeb2e-81ce-46f0-af2d-c73589f658d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Its October 9, 2026 report contains 162 entries for Congressman Himes during the 119th Congress.
## The Issues That Affect Connecticut Families
Here is the website's complete issue-by-issue scorecard:
**Healthcare -- What about affordability? - Jim Scores a C**
Himes supports extending Affordable Care Act subsidies. But what about Medicare Advantage oversight, prescription costs, and expanding benefits for seniors? Families need measurable relief from healthcare expenses.
**Housing and Affordability -- Who pays for the infrastructure? - Jim Scores a C**
Himes supports federal housing incentives. Yet increased development requires roads, sewer capacity, water systems, schools, and other public infrastructure.
Where is Washington's investment in the infrastructure that our communities actually need?
**Immigration -- What happened to enforcement? - Jim does get an A**
Yet, Himes voted against the Laken Riley Act and the SAVE Act. He supports a pathway to citizenship for qualifying DREAMers and Temporary Protected Status holders.
These legislative choices deserve public examination, including their implications for immigration enforcement and election administration.
Jim wants all illegals to become citizens to become future voters.
**Energy -- What about our electric bills? Jim gets an A- on climate not affordable energy**
Himes supports clean-energy incentives and environmental regulations.
But Connecticut households face substantial electricity and heating expenses. What is his plan for expanding reliable generation, improving natural-gas access, and addressing energy affordability?
**Justice and Civil Liberties -- What about constitutional protections? Jim gets a C-**
Himes supported reauthorizing Section 702 of FISA without certain additional warrant protections sought by privacy advocates.
National security matters. So do constitutional liberties. His position deserves scrutiny as this is what our Constitution and our Bill of Rights is all about. Jim's record speaks otherwise.
**Labor - Jim Gets a C+**
His party is no longer the party of the working class.
**Israel -- Jim Gets a C**
Himes has supported maintaining American military assistance to Israel while also supporting humanitarian measures in Gaza and opposing certain sanctions involving the International Criminal Court.
**War & Foreign Policy** \- **Jim Gets a B**
Basically an adequate score.
## And What About Bringing Federal Dollars Back to Connecticut?
After nearly 18 years in Congress, constituents have every reason to ask:
* Where is the federal investment needed for southwestern Connecticut's aging sewer infrastructure?
* What measurable progress has Washington delivered on I-95 congestion?
* How is federal policy helping residents facing high healthcare and energy expenses?
* How much federal funding is returning to our towns to relieve the burden on local taxpayers?

**These are the questions that matter when the television cameras turn off. Also, How Does Jim compare to the rest of Congressional Team from Connecticut? - He ranks 4 out of 5. Yet Courtney has at least brought Jobs to CT with Electric Boat. Himes couldn 't keep the Post Office sorting facility in Stamford.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/da8fea22-ae91-40a2-beae-6b4b3e702c32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## Congress Is Not a Television Studio
Jim Himes has spent years explaining Washington to Connecticut.
It is equally important that he explain what Washington has delivered for Connecticut, especially in his district.
A congressional representative should be evaluated on legislative actions, funding secured, constituent service, and measurable policy results.
Television appearances tell us what a politician says.
**Congressional records tell us what a politician does.**
And Connecticut residents deserve to examine both.
In a state which is totally controlled and mismanaged by the Democrats being the second worst congressman in Connecticut is not what Connecticut's 4th Congressional District should be sending to Congress.
Where it counts, Himes is not on the side of the people. He fails in healthcare, housing and affordability, he is not pro labor, does not support justice and civil liberty, does not support democracy and voting rights does not support voter ID, likes money influencing politics and is not a supporter of Israel's right to defend itself.
Jim puts on a great act pretending to be for the people, but where it counts he does vote in the best interests of the people of Connecticut. Let's send him to Hollywood but not back to Congress.

It is time for change and to send a Doctor to Congress.

[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261010_3.NO1p3P&refcode=em20261010-3&t=1&akid=9450%2E582294%2Ed1qFwr)
Let me be clear: **There is no second place in this race.**
There’s no silver medal, no participation prize – and no “try again next year.” Our race in Ohio will decide Senate control, and I can’t stress enough how high the stakes are.
Second place means rising costs for hardworking families.
Second place means cuts to healthcare coverage so that the wealthiest Americans get more tax breaks.
**Second place means giving Jon Husted two more years of being Trump’s puppet – and it means giving up our best shot at flipping the Senate.**
That’s why I need your help. Right now, we’re tied in the polls, and Republican megadonors are spending a quarter of a BILLION dollars to help Husted surge ahead.
The only way I can fight back is with your immediate help. I’m relying on grassroots support from folks like you to ensure the values and priorities of Ohio working families come in first place on November 3.
**[Will you split $5 right now between my campaign and Chris Pappas to win in Ohio and flip the Senate? In a race this close, every dollar could be the difference between winning and losing.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261010_3.NO1p3P&refcode=em20261010-3&t=2&akid=9450%2E582294%2Ed1qFwr)**

Last year, at least 88 of the biggest corporations in America paid zero dollars in federal corporate income taxes last year — even while posting healthy pretax profits here in the U.S. _**That didn’t happen by accident.**_ It’s the predictable result when politicians cut taxes for big companies and then let the people who profit from those cuts write the rules. Meanwhile, the same interests pushing for tax giveaways are also the ones pouring money into political campaigns and lobbying for loopholes that benefit them. My GOP opponent, Rob Bresnahan, accepts corporate donations from companies like these and continues to sell out NEPA anytime he can pad his portfolio. This is how corporate money in politics works: it buys influence, it shapes policy, and it shields profits from public accountability. You can see the consequences clearly — promises about protecting healthcare or restoring fairness rings hollow when the policies coming out of DC tilt toward special interests instead of families. I’m running for office to change that. I’ll fight to restore transparency, ban corporate PAC donations, and restore public trust by making decisions that are best for our families, not corporations. Peter, it’s Governor Wes Moore.
I will work with anybody. **_But I will bow to nobody._**
I didn’t come from money or prestige. As the son of an immigrant single mother, I came from hard work, community, and an unshakeable belief that _we could do better._
**[If you share that belief, would you split a donation of $25 between our re-election campaign and Heartland Patriots today?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/109655?refcode=em20261010-10990&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10990%2E614464%2E2ZzdG6)**

That history and resilience is why I believe every family deserves a fair shot at work, wages, and wealth — not just survival.

clean_body: Congress poured more than $100 billion into immigration enforcement while working families pay more for everything. | | | Peter, Imagine building your life here for years: working, raising your kids, and contributing to your community. Then immigration agents detain you, and you aren't even allowed to ask a judge to let you go home while your case plays out. That's the policy the Supreme Court just agreed to review.1 Mass deportation doesn't only impact immigrants. When a coworker is locked away, the work falls on everyone else. When a neighbor disappears, families lose paychecks and kids lose a parent at the dinner table. Working families already pay $2,358 a year for mass deportation. Citizenship would mean a $4,300 raise.2 The National Association of Home Builders is sounding the alarm. It says this policy has removed workers from the labor force, forced project cancellations, and eliminated jobs for U.S.-born workers, all during a housing shortage.3 Lower courts have overwhelmingly ruled against the administration's policy. A decision is expected by July.1 We'll be watching, and ready to mobilize, whatever the outcome. Peter,

A little while ago, I spent some time in the Sigourney area meeting with four community members: Nathan, Lucas, Jeff, and Deb.

We talked about building a stronger economy, the investments our rural communities need, and how bureaucracy has kept them from receiving the infrastructure dollars and other federal funding they need and deserve. I told them I will work to cut down on red tape and make sure our rural communities can really thrive.

**I believe a representative's most important responsibility is to listen to the people they serve and fight for the issues that matter to them.** That means showing up in our communities, asking questions, hearing people out, and then taking those concerns back to Washington and acting on them.

**It shouldn't feel like pulling teeth to get your member of Congress to listen, but for too long, Mariannette Miller-Meeks has ignored the people of IA-01.** That's not how representation should work, and I'm determined to change it.

I've spent this campaign talking with Iowans from all walks of life. I can't wait to bring those conversations to Congress and make sure the people of IA-01 have a representative who actually shows up for them.

_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3436%2E259176%2EJThqhr) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3436%2E259176%2EJThqhr)_

[](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/17725?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.09_Flanagan-Native_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS2&t=4&akid=3436%2E259176%2EJThqhr) Peter — in almost 250 years, there’s never been a Native woman serving in the US Senate. **It’s time to change that.**

I’m Peggy Flanagan, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota.

I am Ojibwe and a proud member of the White Earth Nation. My family is the Wolf Clan. The mission of my clan is to never leave anyone behind — and that’s been my guiding principle.

I am the descendant of people who were forced off their land onto the White Earth reservation. I am the relative of residential boarding school survivors. I am the daughter of a man who always spoke truth to power for the good of the Anishinaabe people.

I’m thinking of my daughter — who just got her first jingle dress — and whether or not she will see Indigenous women in all parts of our government.

**Right now, there are _no_ Native voices in the US Senate. _If I win this race, we can change that._** [**It's high time that all our communities have a seat at the table. If you agree, will you pitch in $10 or whatever you can to power my campaign and Blue Amp Action and help me make history?**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/18305?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.09_Flanagan-Native_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS2&t=5&akid=3436%2E259176%2EJThqhr) | [SPLIT $20 >>](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/18306?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.09_Flanagan-Native_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS2&t=6&akid=3436%2E259176%2EJThqhr)
---
Too often, Native voices are ignored or erased in the halls of power..

That’s how we get awful so-called leaders like Donald Trump and J.D. Vance, who called Indigenous Peoples' Day a “fake holiday” and said that Native land was “enemy territory.”.

My Ojibwe name means 'Speaks in a Loud and Clear Voice woman.' So I’m using that voice to call out MAGA extremism — loudly and clearly.
But I can’t do it alone. I need your help to build a campaign strong enough to cut through the noise.[**That’s why I’m personally asking, Peter, will you pitch in a split gift to my campaign to help us make history?**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/18305?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.10.09_Flanagan-Native_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS2&t=7&akid=3436%2E259176%2EJThqhr)

On Friday, in a federal courtroom in Anniston, U.S. District Judge Corey Maze sentenced 28-year-old Eladio Pascual-Gaspar to 31 months in prison for illegal reentry. On any docket, that is a routine case. In his file, it's the last page of a story Washington wrote eleven years earlier.
Here is the arc. In 2015, Pascual-Gaspar crossed the border as an unaccompanied minor. The government handed him to a sponsor and turned him loose -- and, in any sense that matters, stopped watching. In 2021, he pleaded guilty in Mississippi to aiding and abetting an armed robbery. The robbery earned him punishment. The immigration file earned him a deportation, in 2023. Then he walked right back in.
June 2026, Talladega. Police find a 15-year-old -- himself, per court records, in the country illegally -- alone in a car registered to a man named Henry Vegas Mondragon. The car gets towed. A fellow shows up at the lot to claim it, flashing Guatemalan ID under that same made-up name. The ID is fake. So is the name. It is Pascual-Gaspar. Homeland Security Investigations and the Talladega County Drug Task Force built the case; the Justice Department prosecuted it under its Operation Take Back America banner. Friday, Maze made it official: 31 months.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/12a58715-6b94-4c4c-a02a-27d6aeac9fb0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now study the thing, because one man is one data point with a pipeline behind it.
From fiscal 2015 through 2024, the Office of Refugee Resettlement released nearly 700,000 unaccompanied children to sponsors -- almost 28,000 the year Pascual-Gaspar arrived. In FY2024, 89 percent of discharges went to family sponsors, per the Congressional Research Service. The handoff to the sponsor is where the government's attention ends. Not declines. Ends.
You don't have to take my word for it. DHS's own Inspector General found that ICE cannot effectively monitor the location or status of children after release: roughly 31,000 kids released from 2019 to 2023 had missing or incomplete addresses in their files; as of January 2025, about 233,000 had never been served with a notice to appear in immigration court; another 43,000 were served and simply skipped. That is not a border problem. That is a back-office problem -- and it manufactures reentrants by the boatload.
Which brings me to the part people keep missing: this happened in Alabama.
Alabama is one of the reddest states in the union, and in 2011 it passed HB 56, among the most aggressive state immigration laws ever written. Talladega County is not a sanctuary jurisdiction; it is a drug-task-force jurisdiction. Yet none of that state-level toughness mattered, because the pipeline is federal. Washington releases the minor, loses the file, skips the hearing, waits for the robbery, delegates the deportation, then acts surprised at the reentry. A state can pass any law it likes. It cannot opt out of a federal release program. Talladega didn't fail here. The system upstream did -- and the bill landed on an Alabama tow lot, in an Alabama courtroom, with an Alabama 15-year-old sitting in a car registered to an alias.
Credit where due, because Friday proves something else: the back end worked. A federal judge imposed real prison. Section 1326 means the next return carries enhanced felony time. HSI and the local task force caught him -- but only because he got greedy and walked into a tow lot to reclaim a car he'd registered under his fake name. Luck did the rest. A functioning system shouldn't need that luck.
Three fixes would matter more than another press conference. Vet sponsors and follow up on them -- the Inspector General's own recommendation. Serve the paperwork, because 233,000 kids with no notice to appear are the reentrants of 2030. And stop treating reentry after deportation like a paperwork offense. It is a felony, and this man proved the point by treating his own deportation as a suggestion.
There's a smaller tragedy folded inside this one. The kid in the car is fifteen. Eleven years ago, the kid in the pipeline was one too. Same release, same sponsor handoff, same lost file -- the conveyor belt doesn't just deliver men back to us; it recruits the next lap from the current one.
They released him as a kid. They ignored the armed robbery. They deported him once. He came back with a fake name and another teenager in the car. Stop calling that compassion. It is a conveyor belt, and Americans are paying for every lap.

Red-state Alabama has this problem too -- because the conveyor belt is federal. | | | Oct 10 | | | | | | | | | | | | On Friday, in a federal courtroom in Anniston, U.S. District Judge Corey Maze sentenced 28-year-old Eladio Pascual-Gaspar to 31 months in prison for illegal reentry. On any docket, that is a routine case. In his file, it's the last page of a story Washington wrote eleven years earlier. Here is the arc. In 2015, Pascual-Gaspar crossed the border as an unaccompanied minor. The government handed him to a sponsor and turned him loose -- and, in any sense that matters, stopped watching. In 2021, he pleaded guilty in Mississippi to aiding and abetting an armed robbery. The robbery earned him punishment. The immigration file earned him a deportation, in 2023. Then he walked right back in. June 2026, Talladega. Police find a 15-year-old -- himself, per court records, in the country illegally -- alone in a car registered to a man named Henry Vegas Mondragon. The car gets towed. A fellow shows up at the lot to claim it, flashing Guatemalan ID under that same made-up name. The ID is fake. So is the name. It is Pascual-Gaspar. Homeland Security Investigations and the Talladega County Drug Task Force built the case; the Justice Department prosecuted it under its Operation Take Back America banner. Friday, Maze made it official: 31 months. | | ---|---|--- Now study the thing, because one man is one data point with a pipeline behind it. From fiscal 2015 through 2024, the Office of Refugee Resettlement released nearly 700,000 unaccompanied children to sponsors -- almost 28,000 the year Pascual-Gaspar arrived. In FY2024, 89 percent of discharges went to family sponsors, per the Congressional Research Service. The handoff to the sponsor is where the government's attention ends. Not declines. Ends. You don't have to take my word for it. DHS's own Inspector General found that ICE cannot effectively monitor the location or status of children after release: roughly 31,000 kids released from 2019 to 2023 had missing or incomplete addresses in their files; as of January 2025, about 233,000 had never been served with a notice to appear in immigration court; another 43,000 were served and simply skipped. That is not a border problem. That is a back-office problem -- and it manufactures reentrants by the boatload. Which brings me to the part people keep missing: this happened in Alabama. Alabama is one of the reddest states in the union, and in 2011 it passed HB 56, among the most aggressive state immigration laws ever written. Talladega County is not a sanctuary jurisdiction; it is a drug-task-force jurisdiction. Yet none of that state-level toughness mattered, because the pipeline is federal. Washington releases the minor, loses the file, skips the hearing, waits for the robbery, delegates the deportation, then acts surprised at the reentry. A state can pass any law it likes. It cannot opt out of a federal release program. Talladega didn't fail here. The system upstream did -- and the bill landed on an Alabama tow lot, in an Alabama courtroom, with an Alabama 15-year-old sitting in a car registered to an alias. Credit where due, because Friday proves something else: the back end worked. A federal judge imposed real prison. Section 1326 means the next return carries enhanced felony time. HSI and the local task force caught him -- but only because he got greedy and walked into a tow lot to reclaim a car he'd registered under his fake name. Luck did the rest. A functioning system shouldn't need that luck. Three fixes would matter more than another press conference. Vet sponsors and follow up on them -- the Inspector General's own recommendation. Serve the paperwork, because 233,000 kids with no notice to appear are the reentrants of 2030. And stop treating reentry after deportation like a paperwork offense. It is a felony, and this man proved the point by treating his own deportation as a suggestion. There's a smaller tragedy folded inside this one. The kid in the car is fifteen. Eleven years ago, the kid in the pipeline was one too. Same release, same sponsor handoff, same lost file -- the conveyor belt doesn't just deliver men back to us; it recruits the next lap from the current one. They released him as a kid. They ignored the armed robbery. They deported him once. He came back with a fake name and another teenager in the car. Stop calling that compassion. | Letter from the Chair
---
| Friends,
In 2008, Al Franken won Minnesota's U.S. Senate seat by 312 votes. Out of nearly 2.9 million ballots cast, 312 votes decided it. That's fewer people than would fill a high school gym on a Friday night.
That seat gave DC Democrats their 60th vote. Months later, they used it to force Obamacare through the Senate without a single Republican vote. Every family that watched premiums climb and lost the plan they were promised they could keep lived with the result of 312 people who didn't bother to show up.
It can happen here. Too many Republicans believe Nebraska is so red that our vote doesn't matter. But our Second District electoral vote went to Kamala Harris in 2024, just as it went to Joe Biden in 2020 and Barack Obama in 2008. Every time, Republicans told themselves Nebraska was safe.
This November, the stakes are even higher.
Senator Pete Ricketts is facing Dan Osborn, the same "independent" who came within a few points of beating Senator Deb Fischer two years ago. Democrats are putting everything behind Osborn because they know a Nebraska seat could decide control of the U.S. Senate, just like Minnesota did.
Governor Jim Pillen is on the ballot: a businessman and family man who holds Nebraska's conservative values. He's facing a sweet-talking but big-spending liberal who has a record of advocating gender-mutilating surgery on children and keeping boys in girls' sports.
Don Bacon is retiring, leaving the Second District wide open. Our nominee, Brinker Harding, is facing Dark Money Denise Powell, who is heavily funded by the most radical elements of the Democratic Party from outside our state.
We have close races for control of our State Board of Education. There are Board of Regents races that will determine whether conservative, commonsense voices have a say in our cherished University of Nebraska system.
Many seats in our Legislature are up for election. In our Unicameral, it takes 33 votes to break a filibuster. Lose even one or two seats, and real property tax relief stalls. So do our efforts to rein in government spending, protect your Second Amendment rights, and keep parents in charge of their kids' education.
Lower on the ballot, but still important, are public power board seats, Natural Resources District seats, and other races that determine our utility rates and how we spend on Nebraska's land and water resources.
None of that is lost all at once. It slips away one seat, one skipped election at a time.
Make a plan to vote. In-person early voting is open now at your county election office, and mail ballot requests are due October 23. Then bring three people with you: a neighbor, a coworker, a family member.
312 votes changed the country. Yours can too.
Together we win!
In Liberty and in Truth,
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair | Friends, In 2008, Al Franken won Minnesota's U.S. Senate seat by 312 votes. Out of nearly 2.9 million ballots cast, 312 votes decided it. That's fewer people than would fill a high school gym on a Friday night. That seat gave DC Democrats their 60th vote. Months later, they used it to force Obamacare through the Senate without a single Republican vote. Every family that watched premiums climb and lost the plan they were promised they could keep lived with the result of 312 people who didn't bother to show up. It can happen here. Too many Republicans believe Nebraska is so red that our vote doesn't matter. But our Second District electoral vote went to Kamala Harris in 2024, just as it went to Joe Biden in 2020 and Barack Obama in 2008. Every time, Republicans told themselves Nebraska was safe. This November, the stakes are even higher. Senator Pete Ricketts is facing Dan Osborn, the same "independent" who came within a few points of beating Senator Deb Fischer two years ago. Democrats are putting everything behind Osborn because they know a Nebraska seat could decide control of the U.S. Senate, just like Minnesota did. Governor Jim Pillen is on the ballot: a businessman and family man who holds Nebraska's conservative values. He's facing a sweet-talking but big-spending liberal who has a record of advocating gender-mutilating surgery on children and keeping boys in girls' sports. Don Bacon is retiring, leaving the Second District wide open. Our nominee, Brinker Harding, is facing Dark Money Denise Powell, who is heavily funded by the most radical elements of the Democratic Party from outside our state. We have close races for control of our State Board of Education. There are Board of Regents races that will determine whether conservative, commonsense voices have a say in our cherished University of Nebraska system. Many seats in our Legislature are up for election. In our Unicameral, it takes 33 votes to break a filibuster. Lose even one or two seats, and real property tax relief stalls. So do our efforts to rein in government spending, protect your Second Amendment rights, and keep parents in charge of their kids' education. Lower on the ballot, but still important, are public power board seats, Natural Resources District seats, and other races that determine our utility rates and how we spend on Nebraska's land and water resources. None of that is lost all at once. It slips away one seat, one skipped election at a time. Make a plan to vote. In-person early voting is open now at your county election office, and mail ballot requests are due October 23. Then bring three people with you: a neighbor, a coworker, a family member. 312 votes changed the country. Yours can too. Together we win! In Liberty and in Truth, Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party Follow us: ==| ==| ==| == Donate today: Support the NEGOP at == For more information, visit == | | From The Desk of NEGOP Political Director Joe Hagerty... [ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek, while
you're reading this, there are volunteers knocking doors across
Pennsylvania at this very moment.

Saturday is the biggest voter contact day of our week, every week — and
after today, there are only three of them left before Election Day.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/16567?t=1001&akid=586%2E245147%2Er-TI7m ]Each volunteer we can't fully staff and supply is thousands of
conversations that never happen. So Derek,
will you chip in $10 today and help us
make all three weekends we have left count?

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/16567?t=1002&akid=586%2E245147%2Er-TI7m ]Chip in →

Here's what today looks like on the ground.

Organizers were at staging locations before 9AM this morning, handing out
packets and literature. Volunteers who gave up their own Saturday are
working neighborhoods in every corner of the state. Most of them will
knock on doors until dark, come back tomorrow, and do it again.

That's the part Mar-a-Lago money can't replicate,
Derek. Our far-right opponent
can run all the attack ads she wants, but she can’t buy a few thousand
Pennsylvanians who'd rather spend Saturday knocking doors and having one
conversation at a time because they believe in the work we’re doing.

But Derek,
being able to continue this work — having
every organizer on a payroll, getting every piece of literature printed,
and traveling to every county in Pennsylvania costs money.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/16567?t=1003&akid=586%2E245147%2Er-TI7m ]So Derek, if
you care about the future of our democracy, please chip in
$10
today to help us make the most of these last three Saturdays we get and

must-win race.

subject: We just added 8 new races to our target list

body:
I wanted to make sure you saw our announcement from earlier this week.
#
Hi there, Craig here, Political Director at Swing Left.
I wanted to make sure you saw our announcement from earlier this week.
With less than a month to go until Election Day, we’ve been closely monitoring swing districts and state races across the country. Based on what we’ve been seeing—changes in the races, an all-time low on Trump’s approval rating, and more—**we made the decision to add 6 more U.S. House races and 2 more governor’s races to our list of targets for this November:**
We’re in a sprint to the finish in these final few weeks, and Democrats have the opportunity to win big across the country—but only if they have the resources to get voters to the polls.
If you’d like to help, you can [**click here to donate to our Flip the House Fund**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2628?t=1&akid=3094%2E1562180%2E3WeVz6) or [**click here to donate to our Win In The States Fund**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2629?t=2&akid=3094%2E1562180%2E3WeVz6) today.
Make sure to read below for more information about why we’re adding these specific races. And thank you, as always, for everything you’re doing to build long-term power for Democrats.
Craig
Political Director, Swing Left
\-------- Forwarded message --------
From: Swing Left
Subject: Our final map expansion before Election Day!
Hi there,
As we enter the last four weeks of the election, [Democrats are positioned to do well](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2432?t=3&akid=3094%2E1562180%2E3WeVz6) on Election Day. But the fact remains that Republicans have an outside spending money advantage, and they’re using it to reserve millions of dollars of ad space to attack Democrats and distract from their unpopular agenda and the Trump administration’s blatant corruption.
That makes these final weeks especially important. That’s when many voters will start paying attention to races and when campaigns will make their final push to reach voters.
The Swing Left political team has been closely tracking campaigns across the country, looking at polling, voting trends, fundraising, and what we’re seeing on the ground. Based on that analysis, we believe several additional House and Governor’s races could benefit from an investment now.
As a result, **we’re expanding our Must-Win target list to include 6 more U.S. House races and 2 more Governor’s races!**
Here are all the new races we’re adding to our map:
* **New Hampshire’s 1st Congressional District, Democrat Stefany Shaheen (Must-Hold):** After a competitive primary, Shaheen now faces a wealthy opponent who can self-fund his campaign in this historically swingy district. We need to make sure she has the resources and support needed to overcome her opponent’s money.

* **California's 6th Congressional District, Democrat Dr. Richard Pan (Must-Flip):** Dr. Pan is running against Republican-turned-independent Rep. Kevin Kiley in this newly drawn district. The district was redrawn under Proposition 50 to create a stronger opportunity for Democrats, but Kiley is well-funded and mounting a serious campaign to take this seat.

* **Florida’s 13th Congressional District, Democrat Leela Gray (Must-Flip):** Gray is challenging controversial Republican Rep. Anna Paulina Luna in this light red district. Polls show a tight contest, but Gray entered the race late and needs to catch up on fundraising.

* **Florida’s 22nd Congressional District, Democrat Pia Dandiya (Must-Flip):** Republicans redrew this district earlier this year to lean red, but Democrats still have a path to compete. If the 2020 presidential results were applied to the new district lines, President Biden would have won the district by 3%. In this political environment, Dandiya is running a strong campaign to hold on to this seat and overcome the Republican gerrymander.

* **Kentucky’s 6th Congressional District, Democrat Zach Dembo (Must-Flip):** This open seat leans red, but Democratic Governor Andy Beshear carried it by double digits in his 2023 reelection campaign. Dembo, a former military prosecutor and policy advisor to Gov. Beshear, is running against a vulnerable Republican former state legislator who only moved back to Kentucky to run here.

* **Montana’s 1st Congressional District, Democrat Sam Forstag (Must-Flip):** Former smokejumper Sam Forstag is running against right-wing radio host Aaron Flint for this open seat in western Montana that voted for former Democratic Senator Jon Tester. After winning the Democratic primary with an impressive ground game, Forstag is well-positioned to flip this seat.

[**If you’d like to support Swing Left and the Democratic nominees in all of our most critical red-to-blue House races across the country, click here to make a donation to the Flip the House Fund.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2628?t=4&akid=3094%2E1562180%2E3WeVz6)
* **Alaska Governors’ Race, Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (Must-Flip):** Independent analysts at _Cook Political Report_ just moved this race to “Toss Up” as Democrats have consolidated behind former State Rep. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, who is facing three conservative Republican candidates. Alaska’s ranked-choice voting means Republicans must ensure that voters rank the other Republican candidates as their second and third choice in order to consolidate the Republican vote–also known as their “rank the red” strategy. That creates an opening for Kreiss-Tomkins to consolidate Democrats, independents, and even moderate Republicans.

* **Texas Governors’ Race, Democrat Gina Hinojosa (Must-Flip):** Polling has shown an increasingly competitive race between state Rep. Gina Hinojosa and 11-year Republican incumbent Governor Greg Abbott. As Trump and GOP Senate nominee Ken Paxton drag down Republicans in Texas, Abbott faces a tough political environment and backlash over positions on issues like data centers. His enormous cash advantage in this expensive state means Hinojosa needs immediate support to stay competitive.

[**You can support Hinojosa and Kreiss-Tomkins by making a donation to the Win in the States Fund today.** ](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2629?t=5&akid=3094%2E1562180%2E3WeVz6)
With just 4 weeks left, we’re in a sprint to the finish—and we can’t thank you enough for everything you’re doing to help Democrats win in as many places as possible on November 3rd!
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261010-1&t=6&refcode2=3094_1562180_3WeVz6&akid=3094%2E1562180%2E3WeVz6)

The district was redrawn under Proposition 50 to create a stronger opportunity for Democrats, but Kiley is well-funded and mounting a serious campaign to take this seat. Florida’s 13th Congressional District, Democrat Leela Gray (Must-Flip): Gray is challenging controversial Republican Rep. Anna Paulina Luna in this light red district. Polls show a tight contest, but Gray entered the race late and needs to catch up on fundraising. Florida’s 22nd Congressional District, Democrat Pia Dandiya (Must-Flip): Republicans redrew this district earlier this year to lean red, but Democrats still have a path to compete. If the 2020 presidential results were applied to the new district lines, President Biden would have won the district by 3%. In this political environment, Dandiya is running a strong campaign to hold on to this seat and overcome the Republican gerrymander. Kentucky’s 6th Congressional District, Democrat Zach Dembo (Must-Flip): This open seat leans red, but Democratic Governor Andy Beshear carried it by double digits in his 2023 reelection campaign. Dembo, a former military prosecutor and policy advisor to Gov. Beshear, is running against a vulnerable Republican former state legislator who only moved back to Kentucky to run here. Montana’s 1st Congressional District, Democrat Sam Forstag (Must-Flip): Former smokejumper Sam Forstag is running against right-wing radio host Aaron Flint for this open seat in western Montana that voted for former Democratic Senator Jon Tester. After winning the Democratic primary with an impressive ground game, Forstag is well-positioned to flip this seat. Alaska Governors’ Race, Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (Must-Flip): Independent analysts at Cook Political Report just moved this race to “Toss Up” as Democrats have consolidated behind former State Rep. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, who is facing three conservative Republican candidates. Alaska’s ranked-choice voting means Republicans must ensure that voters rank the other Republican candidates as their second and third choice in order to consolidate the Republican vote–also known as their “rank the red” strategy. That creates an opening for Kreiss-Tomkins to consolidate Democrats, independents, and even moderate Republicans. Texas Governors’ Race, Democrat Gina Hinojosa (Must-Flip): Polling has shown an increasingly competitive race between state Rep. Gina Hinojosa and 11-year Republican incumbent Governor Greg Abbott. As Trump and GOP Senate nominee Ken Paxton drag down Republicans in Texas, Abbott faces a tough political environment and backlash over positions on issues like data centers. His enormous cash advantage in this expensive state means Hinojosa needs immediate support to stay competitive. Fellow American,

This is the first and last email I'll ever send you.

You see, I'm a little unsure about opening up to you this way.

**But the deck is stacked against us, my back is against the wall, and your response to this message will decide everything.**

My name is Pat Harrigan. You don't know me, but I'm a Green Beret veteran from North Carolina. I graduated from West Point, and I served 18 months in combat.

After that, my wife and I started a firearm parts company from our double-wide trailer - and grew it to become a successful, job-creating business. And most important of all, I'm the dad of two beautiful girls.

**I'm honored to have won my race for North Carolina's 10th Congressional District in 2024, and I'm proud to work alongside President Trump to make our nation great again.**

With President Trump in the Oval Office and House and Senate Majorities in Congress, we're more equipped than ever to get our country back on track. The only thing we're missing is the resources to keep going.

**[That’s why I’m humbly asking if you’ll chip in just a few bucks today.](http://links.harriganfornc.com/u/click?_t=687026f8d8f7415aa539c5385c376b1f&_m=1f32600b4326418190778f6270977b2e&_e=sSisNAnjNZh8iu4M1N1L1htHNCmwr06WW5OOoJXKfD6d1JbGmsUFtrdmWXHnoabQBsK9KUP_QG8bnIhvgYXGBt56ohd3GvU_YwL_EnHN9NHhcfWatpsxNFYXIDDB-F1UPEtzTFx-l02OPnw5YSTXbG5WUof70H7UdaZ6xT51RMXJLSgpu9QCq7oXIj31RKfSoQwM6zkElpa4Vjz3KQCM0JBZ1ebZUpP5oq3PAp8dfSNSAmatXc1VjpOt5RSG4dPtNsjPBdBtMt8W5O4wn73ag_fTdgOoNGbjbrwVWNJscn_eWwybp39CNdsiu9wFcnH0VQsKHDljZh2ZvuWcQsxYm3DLsqgYblvySTQjIQ5mAg-bMeyiBcGfJhA3DGBCq-IF4Ec2pb2TtIEFqEkg_s5nl9muNNIthSBzWQY5FLNpJeOHcnqvfHiUBgrxymPx-Wk-W7IGOt4yCNRtfH90Ck29VbbusU2WVBw3HPpN3b8WDT0sJzZyQmzAL3MHOXshVvV4tWZQWii0vONkoQDjjVDJiETxQh_hvw5b2zmYX5kxbXI%3D)**

I'm not the kind of guy who asks for help, but running a grassroots campaign is tough - **really, really tough.**

Friend, Some of Trump’s Big Brutal Bill cuts are**going into effect this month** and in the coming months. If you use SNAP, Medicaid, CHIP (the Children's Health Insurance Program), or Affordable Care Act (ACA) subsidies to make your health insurance more affordable, _please check out the overview of information below the first hyperlink_. **Republicans’ cuts to federal nutrition and healthcare programs were the deepest in our country’s history, stripping life-saving assistance from millions of Americans and their families.** And more are to come, unless Congress acts. With millions of families already struggling to afford basic needs such as food and healthcare, and prices on the rise, we must demand Congress act soon. [**Please sign on to tell Congress: Reverse the cuts to SNAP and Medicaid, reverse the cost shift to states, expand rather than reduce ACA subsidies,****_and_****take action toward universal healthcare and universal school meals for all.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39Vp4gkIh90ovDrixVFaBLcMBRAa14K-TIknHiCdVRe2E3tP4TgNpoc8ORGGD_ty3M095xtgu8eOm2r9w4WtkXpuRaiNZAFVOdDtakUpkiWTAyo7X8msSSzcXm4zKt7pdPDC0AYAJy1zG7xOfmOW3xth0o7NYa9J5sCfWPgHIfsg4oDSKJJWGTq9vxJV2lwJZl-QQB1pqhyFO1AG-M3PBZYu_18cpG-ad8aMm0q-QgA06XDJFxIRnLpani9MbBdrn_DtU4o7qx3v03c7zUhRz0KMd7Ri0KYw_B4WBBb8TJ8pYxeMINpMgDFespLhb9-WLWqyVWVag6ibX3MNYaKEJddtw8_NeuBrZ1jHhrux4GaRgGJ9tSyz8zJcAe3X67-Ton9sS-vvxia5ApqQldu85tQ7bdBQpxfklHhQOTFMIId70GgmdVbZBcl3kxyTKKQU8w-K7MlhR7jTYJ14mvQ_iQQYSS1qK6MG5kvgcwu0LrVfo8eON9F-tCVjqoyiIEtsESerKxqscpuX8i0Vh-qOZeq27UqMiEU99sHQOjsLXaKb8KKBiHOx26KmNW9DdS1oMw/4ur/xGiY3KmSSqip64z9cccaJw/h1/h001.WXwqxIRflIMlYAKJMuKroh-V489KiMGgGeJm6nIL9N8) | [SIGN ON](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39Vp4gkIh90ovDrixVFaBLcMBRAa14K-TIknHiCdVRe2E3tP4TgNpoc8ORGGD_ty3M095xtgu8eOm2r9w4WtkXpm7IKacYcDrWTovipU3el-RhRwdqNfva99AKtGPvMhW3sSC9aUa9RMe0e1k2xo08qhZLf1rNIoeP9Rl7_mx-M--FwUSCtnKJF5iNauLWxm60YJ6TXxoYYmhMszaf8sWpPojnyui4g924KHvjX_XwyU5jLfhkcr6QayNpLSDRbuxW63vte7XN7ppIIsGRcdzVyfW8wH4-ai9iU4BUWyYqcocX_uT07yVYLTLC3ARAy16R1ZZwubRY-njggZyx0wo411D9q_vJOvYD778zpy6IhJDYDW48N5x7QwUvmA3-04qGep2M0IyCUMl58OwgKVBKGrMzke6aZB4frLtLBTvK7PBglTPRBKBhCT0FVyPD_MkwaUn4jLtlx6JwwXq9604f-cL2LgXHQpfOtfKhLPrX7MHqHZ3ey0xaCBHS6e4Losz4Q0fPDVlNXDMpK51V6eZuYTJuth79wRdlQt8036v-OUN6HW3Wj0jLEoVPRuohTLFM/4ur/xGiY3KmSSqip64z9cccaJw/h2/h001.o8C3IXgd76gwiTHYRd2r9AehEQwobyDE68gumL6ro70)

**Here are the changes happening this month and the next few months, by early 2027:**
> Many recipients of **SNAP food assistance now face more requirements** to work, volunteer, or go to school for more time to be able to keep their benefits — including people who are 55-64 years old, people with 14-17 year-old children, and unhoused people. People will also need to**manually renew their SNAP**(food stamps), which may have different names depending on your state.
> The costs of administering SNAP are also going up, and now the **federal government is forcing states to pay even more than before to administer SNAP to their residents.** Some states can’t pay; some will pass along this cost to struggling local governments.
> (My state of MI has set aside and approved $170 million for this, but that money could be invested in our communities in other ways, such as building affordable housing and getting lead out of our water.)
> In addition, some previously eligible non-citizens (like refugees) are **losing access to SNAP and**** _Affordable Care Act_****(ACA) subsidies** that help cover the cost of health insurance. And for some immigrants, it will be even harder to access Medicaid, CHIP, and Medicare.
> **If you get ACA subsidies for your health insurance through your state’s exchange or marketplace, please pay attention in this year’s re-enrollment period:** Some people will get a smaller subsidy, some people’s subsidies will be cancelled, and some states are dropping certain plans — so you may need to change your plan, which may affect which of your prescriptions or providers are covered.
> Work reporting requirements for Medicaid eligibility are also going up in every state by next January, when people will also need to prove their eligibility every 6 months.
In the richest country in the world, no one should go hungry, go bankrupt from medical emergencies, or die because they can’t get healthcare.

clean_body: As prices rise and federal assistance shrinks, families urgently need more support. | | | Friend, Some of Trump’s Big Brutal Bill cuts aregoing into effect this month and in the coming months. If you use SNAP, Medicaid, CHIP (the Children's Health Insurance Program), or Affordable Care Act (ACA) subsidies to make your health insurance more affordable, please check out the overview of information below the first hyperlink. Republicans’ cuts to federal nutrition and healthcare programs were the deepest in our country’s history, stripping life-saving assistance from millions of Americans and their families. And more are to come, unless Congress acts. With millions of families already struggling to afford basic needs such as food and healthcare, and prices on the rise, we must demand Congress act soon. | Here are the changes happening this month and the next few months, by early 2027: Many recipients of SNAP food assistance now face more requirements to work, volunteer, or go to school for more time to be able to keep their benefits — including people who are 55-64 years old, people with 14-17 year-old children, and unhoused people. People will also need tomanually renew their SNAP(food stamps), which may have different names depending on your state. The costs of administering SNAP are also going up, and now the federal government is forcing states to pay even more than before to administer SNAP to their residents. Some states can’t pay; some will pass along this cost to struggling local governments. (My state of MI has set aside and approved $170 million for this, but that money could be invested in our communities in other ways, such as building affordable housing and getting lead out of our water.) In addition, some previously eligible non-citizens (like refugees) are losing access to SNAP and Affordable Care Act(ACA) subsidies that help cover the cost of health insurance. And for some immigrants, it will be even harder to access Medicaid, CHIP, and Medicare. If you get ACA subsidies for your health insurance through your state’s exchange or marketplace, please pay attention in this year’s re-enrollment period: Some people will get a smaller subsidy, some people’s subsidies will be cancelled, and some states are dropping certain plans — so you may need to change your plan, which may affect which of your prescriptions or providers are covered. Work reporting requirements for Medicaid eligibility are also going up in every state by next January, when people will also need to prove their eligibility every 6 months. In the richest country in the world, no one should go hungry, go bankrupt from medical emergencies, or die because they can’t get healthcare. Thank you for continuing to push our leaders to serve the American people, and to move with the urgency that our communities deserve. Instead of spending more on war than any other country in the world, we need to invest in our people’s urgent needs. Together we’ll keep pushing more lawmakers to support transformative programs. We’ll keep trying to fix the affordability crisis and guarantee our human rights to food, healthcare, housing, and beyond. With you in the fight for better, Rashida Rashida Tlaib for Congress PO Box 32777 Detroit, MI 48232 | Paid for by Rashida Tlaib for Congress | | Sent via .
