name: Carole King
subject: We need Chris in the Senate.
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261010_2.BQ52Je&refcode=em20261010-2&t=1001&akid=9430%2E582294%2Ew5Y8WI ]Carole King

Hi, it’s
Carole King 🎶, and I personally wrote this email.

Chris Pappas has been serving New Hampshire’s first district in the U.S.
House of Representatives. Now he’s running to serve every Granite Stater
in the U.S. Senate.

I know Chris personally. He is worthy.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261010_2.BQ52Je&refcode=em20261010-2&t=1002&akid=9430%2E582294%2Ew5Y8WI ]If that’s all you need to read to support Chris’s campaign, click here
to donate now, and have a great rest of your day!

John E. Sununu is Chris’s opponent. If elected, he would likely join other
Senate Republicans in voting for whatever the person in the White House
wants no matter how irrational or illogical or corrupt.

And if an opening occurred on the Supreme Court, Sununu would likely
confirm the president’s nominee for another justice to take more of our
rights away.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261010_2.BQ52Je&refcode=em20261010-2&t=1003&akid=9430%2E582294%2Ew5Y8WI ]Will you give $1, $5, or whatever you can afford right now to help
Chris earn the votes of more people in New Hampshire?

Chris Pappas will vote to lift the weight of worries that the president
keeps adding to and that the Republican Senate majority has enabled.

And the Republican Senate majority has failed to stop the president from
spending OUR tax dollars building vanity projects, destroying buildings
that belong to all of us, and profiting from the power of his office.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261010_2.BQ52Je&refcode=em20261010-2&t=1004&akid=9430%2E582294%2Ew5Y8WI ]We need Chris in the Senate to say NO to the president’s whiplash
whims.

We don’t know whether Sununu would have voted for the resolution directing
the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran. But
we do know that Chris Pappas has consistently voted YES to bring our
military family members home.

John E. Sununu and his family appear to have a close relationship with
power and money and maybe not as close with everyday people.

Chris Pappas IS everyday people. And that’s why he needs our help to pay
for gas to travel around the state and earn the votes of Granite Staters
wherever they are.

Will you join me in helping Chris reach more voters?
[If your number isn’t in a box, click OTHER and enter your amount.]

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261010_2.BQ52Je&amount=5&refcode=em20261010-2&t=1023&akid=9430%2E582294%2Ew5Y8WI ]Donate $5 »

Chris is
gaining momentum — but the super-wealthy Republican donors are spending
even more money to turn their wave of negative ads into an October
tsunami.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261010_2.BQ52Je&refcode=em20261010-2&t=1024&akid=9430%2E582294%2Ew5Y8WI ]Will you help Chris’s campaign build more momentum?

Whether you donate or not, here are two other ways you can support Chris
for free.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/695?t=1025&akid=9430%2E582294%2Ew5Y8WI ]Vote.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/signup/take_action_pappas_campaign/?source=em20261010-2&t=1026&akid=9430%2E582294%2Ew5Y8WI ]Volunteer.

I know it’s hard to feel hopeful with so many people
struggling, and it’s even harder if
you’re among them. But hope may lie in the growing movement to replace
corruption and depravity with hope and humanity.

Thank you for participating in whatever ways you can. We can do this.

With my best wishes to you and your family,

- Carole

Carole King is a singer-songwriter, author, and activist. Her
distinctions include a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award, a Kennedy
Center Honor, and double-induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
Now Carole is using her platform to help elect candidates who are
running to lift and improve the lives of their fellow Americans. And she
really did write this email.

People ask me all the time why I left the Republican Party. They expect a simple answer. A single moment. A breaking point. There wasn't one. New Mexico families deserve a tax code that works for them — not one that gives the most profitable corporations another way to avoid paying their fair share. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141134345/652561759/-272948131?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20261010_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMGVlOGJiMi1jM2M0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=K3iQY451ze-fmm_iGZwXEbu2AYWyrz97PR1o1UCxgMw=&emci=898456f0-4ec3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=f0ee8bb2-c3c4-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=252045)
---
Friend, At a time when New Mexico families are feeling the squeeze from rising energy costs, the last thing we should be doing is handing the biggest oil and gas companies outdated tax breaks to produce energy overseas. But that’s exactly what our tax code allows. From 2017 to 2025, major U.S. oil companies paid **$135 BILLION in foreign taxes while paying just $29 billion in U.S. taxes.** At the same time, these same companies continue to rake in billions in profits. _That’s not fair to you — the taxpayers who follow the rules and still get the raw end of the deal. _ The American people deserve a tax code that works for them — _not_ one that gives the most profitable corporations another way to avoid paying their fair share. **That’s why I introduced a bill that would close these outdated loopholes and make sure major oil and gas companies pay their fair share right here in the United States.** Our tax code should not reward companies for investing overseas while American families and small businesses are struggling with higher energy costs at home. We should be strengthening American energy independence, supporting good-paying jobs here in our communities, and investing in a more affordable and reliable energy future. **If these corporations can afford to make billions in profits, they can afford to pay what they owe.** And I’m going to keep fighting to make sure they do for folks in New Mexico and across the country. [**Will you add your name to support my work to ensure oil and gas companies pay their fair share in the U.S. — _not_ abroad?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141134346/652561760/1405009654?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20261010_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMGVlOGJiMi1jM2M0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=K3iQY451ze-fmm_iGZwXEbu2AYWyrz97PR1o1UCxgMw=&emci=898456f0-4ec3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=f0ee8bb2-c3c4-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=252045) | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141134349/652561763/1405009654?refcode=AU_MTH_EG_GEN_PET_AC_20261010_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS84OTA0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMGVlOGJiMi1jM2M0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=K3iQY451ze-fmm_iGZwXEbu2AYWyrz97PR1o1UCxgMw=&emci=898456f0-4ec3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=f0ee8bb2-c3c4-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=252045)

Hey folks,
I'm genuinely sick to my stomach over this one.
Pete Hegseth is reportedly planning to livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, the man responsible for the horrific 2009 Fort Hood shooting. And somehow, the most disturbing part isn't just the proposed execution. It's how excited Hegseth seems to be about turning someone's death into a public spectacle.
I believe America is better than this. And I think we need to have a serious conversation about what happens when cruelty becomes the point.
Here's what we get into:
* [**00:00:53**] Pete Hegseth discusses the proposed firing squad execution, and his reaction is absolutely chilling.
* [**00:03:19**] I break down Hegseth's World War II rhetoric and why glorifying violence isn't the same thing as showing strength.
* [**00:05:01**] Glenn Greenwald raises a disturbing question about human rights, public executions, and what America is becoming.
* [**00:07:35**] Senator Mark Kelly condemns the proposed livestream and calls for Hegseth's immediate removal.
* [**00:11:36**] Senator Jon Ossoff delivers a devastating assessment of Hegseth's leadership, and I explain why this fight is so personal.

This conversation is about more than Pete Hegseth or the death penalty. It's about the kind of country we want to live in. We can demand accountability for horrific crimes without abandoning our humanity. We can believe in justice without celebrating brutality. And we can fight for an America built on compassion, dignity, and basic decency. Peter,
With just four days left until our last FEC deadline before Election Day and a $3 million goal to reach, [**_I’m personally asking you to make your first donation to my campaign_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1627&amount=5&t=8&akid=4397%2E124072%2E-ekO3r) to help us close the gap in time.
Back when I ran for Governor in 2016, all the numbers and polls seemed to be in our favor – but I ended up winning by just 0.22% of the vote, and President Trump carried North Carolina in the presidential election.
Ten years later, I’m up against his handpicked candidate in the race experts say will decide Senate control, and the predictions appear to be on our side once again.
**Peter, if I learned anything from 2016, it’s that we cannot take this race for granted.**
[**_Before Wednesday's critical deadline, will you chip in $5 for the first time to make sure we have the resources to fight back, flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1627&amount=5&t=9&akid=4397%2E124072%2E-ekO3r)

The Democracy Champions we’ve endorsed will fight hard for Georgia families, including by working to stop racist voting maps and voter suppression policies.

Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 24 days. If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=1&akid=9808%2E22930333%2EzvAlfg). With **only 24 days remaining until Election Day** , you might be tempted to think our campaign is winding down and packing up, but that is definitely **not** the case!
We will be knocking on doors every single day leading up to November 3, and we still have the potential to reach **thousands of unique households** in Tennessee's 1st District through our ads on regular TV and streaming.
Thanks for reading Kristi for Congress News & Updates! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.

Here's a snapshot of what your contributions have helped us do in just **3 days** of streaming ads - you helped us reach over **16,000 unique households** in the district! We need to keep that up for the remaining days of the campaign so that Kristi's name stays fresh on the mind of independent and on-the-fence voters!
[I've Read Enough! Donation Page, Please!](https://substack.com/redirect/ed481660-bd46-4b15-b6df-7b232172ebe0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We hate to keep asking, but **the finish line is in sight** , and the last thing we want to do is wake up on November 4 and wonder if **just $100 more** would have helped us get the votes we needed.
We think this race is going to be a lot closer than people imagine. **We believe we can win it.** We're seeing and hearing evidence on the ground.
But we only win with **your continued support** in these final, crucial days. If you've been waiting for the right time to donate to this movement, it is absolutely **RIGHT NOW**. And that's why we're inviting you to **JOIN THE CLUB:**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ed481660-bd46-4b15-b6df-7b232172ebe0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

**The 435 Club** , to be precise! There are 435 elected members in the U.S. House of Representatives, and we want to be sure Kristi Burke is one of them come November 3! We need to raise **$4,350** by Sunday night! That's just four days from now! Here's what we've raised so far:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c5c900bc-176f-45ae-8dfd-7f654cadacf2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
You can join the club by donating one of three amounts:
* $4.35
* $43.50
* $435

Donate one of these amounts, and **you 'll officially be in the club**! And to thank you for this generous donation, we're going to send out a special, secret link to a **group video call with Kristi** so that she can thank express her gratitude face to face, **for just this group of donors**!
[Join The 435 Club Now](https://substack.com/redirect/ed481660-bd46-4b15-b6df-7b232172ebe0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We'll send out date and time information on that call after the fundraiser is complete!
**ONE LAST THING:** We have two generous donors who have agreed to **match** donations **up to $500 each**. So if we raise our goal of $4,350 by Sunday, we'll add another $1,000 for a **total of $5,350**!
[What are you waiting for? Click!](https://substack.com/redirect/ed481660-bd46-4b15-b6df-7b232172ebe0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We can win this if we overcome self-fulfilling prophecies. Will you help us get across the finish line? Can you dig a little deeper to get these ads and campaign materials piping into even more households across Northeast Tennessee?
Let's do this together! Share the [donation link](https://substack.com/redirect/ed481660-bd46-4b15-b6df-7b232172ebe0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with everyone you know!

Lower courts had said immigrants must be allowed to raise objections
before they're put on a plane to a third country. Six justices wiped that
protection away in an unsigned order. No opinion. No explanation.

The Court hasn't even decided whether the policy is legal. It won't hear
arguments until December. Until then, the deportation flights keep taking
off.

And this isn't the first time. The same conservative majority cleared the
way for these flights last year too, allowing Trump to send 25,000 people
to about two dozen different countries.^1

This is what a captured Court looks like. Not a check on presidential
power. An extension of it.

The Roberts Court has become a rubber stamp for Trump's authoritarianism.

happen before it bothers to rule. It has to be reformed.

It’s been a little over a year since Donald Trump and his MAGA majority in Congress defunded public broadcasting.

Since then, public broadcasting organizations have been exploring ways to survive – and rural communities have been affected the most.

That's Deidre Henderson, Utah's Republican lieutenant governor, describing what her state is hearing from Washington about foreign threats to the midterms. U.S. spy agencies expect Russia to spread disinformation again to make Americans distrust the results. China and Iran are active too, and AI is making the lies cheaper to produce. Election officials should be hearing about this as it happens. Here's what happened instead: **CISA, the agency that warns states about these threats, laid off nearly a third of its staff in early 2025. It has had three acting directors and still no permanent one.** The Foreign Malign Influence Center, which tracked foreign disinformation, was shut down. **In July, Trump fired the two Democrats on the Election Assistance Commission. The last commissioner, a Republican, resigned.** Federal election security money for states fell from $55 million in 2024 to $15 million in 2025. The federal government finally released a midterm security plan on September 24. A former CISA election official summed it up: "The best parts of this plan are still too late to be useful. Ballots are live in every state." **To be clear, intelligence officials have seen no sign that anyone can tamper with voting machines or vote counts. subject: A scalpel, a confiscation list, and a focus group

body:
Her base has a doorman. Mine has a dog on the porch.

| [](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.-eUvNtRr4UAQLvg)
---
[A radical Democrat wants my job.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett._ungo2WhPJYB2aIltY6YA)
I won't say her name. She's got an army of folks saying it for her, and not one of them could find Knoxville on a map.
---
[](https://trk.email.tim-burchett._VavsrRwBaZfxclQ)
---
Washington. New York. San Francisco. That's her base. That's her people. That's who's writing the checks - fat (or as the libs say, “pleasantly plump”) ones.
She's betting on one thing: that y’all won't look too close before November.
So let's look closely.
* Abortion: Not "reproductive healthcare." Not "choice." Not whatever focus-grouped label they're hiding behind this week.
* Trans surgeries on children: Kids too young for a tattoo. Too young for a beer. Too young to rent a car. Old enough, she reckons, for a scalpel.
* Gun Control: They'll call it "common sense" right up until somebody's reading names off a confiscation list. I'd bet the farm mine's at the top.

That's her agenda. Here's mine:
* I'll continue to chainsaw Washington's spending addiction as chairman of the DOGE subcommittee.
* I'll defend the Second Amendment as the God-given right it is — not a privilege some bureaucrat hands out.
* And I'll continue standing up for Tennessee values in a city that treats them like a punchline at a cocktail party.

That's the contrast in this race. Ain't close or complicated.
But I'd be doing you wrong to sugarcoat this, Peter: [a good record doesn't win elections by itself anymore.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.)
They've got the donors, consultants in three time zones. and a machine built to swallow districts like ours whole and never even burp.
The only thing between them and my seat is patriots like you, Peter.
[Please, chip in a few bucks right now and show them East Tennessee isn't a prize sitting on a shelf with a price tag hanging off it](https://trk.email.tim-burchett._IAhpQ).
---

Thank y'all for sending me here,

Friend, I was in a crowded coffee shop in Topeka a few weeks ago listening to Kansans talk about their challenges, dreams and hopes for the future.

While I was there, I shared the most fundamental message of my campaign: **Remember to be a good neighbor.** You don’t have to agree with someone to love them. In fact, our system works best when we disagree, because then we can find a compromise that addresses the concerns of both sides.

clean_body: The dubbed "Stop Nick Shirley Act" was made to stop me. | | | | | | | Friend, There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does. Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Friend: it makes it harder for anyone -- me included -- to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent. I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning. Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General -- the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Friend. That's the system protecting itself. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Friend: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place. I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them. Since LMF is a 501(c)3, your gift is tax-deductible , and it can be made anonymously if that's what you'd prefer. Friend, they can pass all the laws they want. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that's why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech -- and that's why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue! For the truth, Nick Shirley P.S. -- A California assemblyman is already asking the DOJ to intervene against this law. My mom worked hard to provide for our family, and when I was 12 years old, I started folding laundry at our apartment complex to help make ends meet.
Those experiences taught me the value of hard work, responsibility, and showing up for the people who count on you.
At 18, I earned an appointment to West Point. I later served as an Army Engineer Officer, graduated from Ranger School, and was honored to receive a Bronze Star during the Gulf War.
After my military service, Margaret and I built our lives here in Colorado. We've raised three daughters, built a small business that now employs more than 120 Coloradans, and spent decades serving our community however we could.

name: Noelle Damico from The Workers Circle via OnePA
subject: How do we stop ICE?
body:
| |
---
Peter, three people with strong habeas cases are sitting in ICE detention right now, and every hour we wait is another chance for them to disappear... Here's the situation: All three are facing deportation. None of them has a lawyer. If ICE moves them to another facility or puts them on a deportation flight before an attorney can file a habeas claim on their behalf, their families may not even know where they've gone. That's why OnePA is joining forces with The Workers Circle this week. **Together, we need to raise $15,000 immediately to get all three attorneys who will file habeas cases.** [**Will you fight back against the deportation regime by splitting a $10, $25, or even $50 donation to the Freedom Advocates program?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqu-wUwIZ511oDywi-RcGpMm0-1_75ztOiSo5PpJdSF8Z2Jrd3qJXpz8uBv9Y5JBP2Xv-krwZU0OPV6mvVlwbPgUWoYu8TqWXzz_IcCePFzQ4y6hUQxwGZBjJ4jfVOTssNTVaz_6CU_HnhbdksSZPvuXm7b-vhirJDw4n7-YcurSgsDZBAmMaP8h5QVIlT822OTU2JzVZ7d1O-gtUytH4wd1w-bR68oaVFnIeG9vV9ylYXcIOAbYNtDonljFAUKrJuPdwjQk4eGlXAcSgWR76uizvHkT1rdJeA3elFAcpfXWIA/4ur/HSL1z9JMQrGdf_3d7U_lmQ/h0/h001.e_i2f5pIXUM6NzXejgRp0oguAcqA8xlSl5zW3TtJ31k) _Last month, with no announcement, ICE quietly stopped listing people with final deportation orders in its online detainee locator._ That's the database families and lawyers rely on to find someone in custody. More than 16,000 people in ICE detention are now missing from it. Lawyers search for their clients and come up empty. Families call facility after facility. Meanwhile, ICE moves people from one detention center to another, and deports people, often with no warning at all.**Immigration lawyers say that for someone with a final order, even a few hours can make the difference between being deported and getting a judge to step in.** This is serious enough that last week, human rights groups asked the United Nations panel that investigates enforced disappearances to intervene. DHS insists it isn't disappearing anyone. But when the government hides where it's holding people and rushes to deport them before anyone can find them, what else would you call it? ICE is counting on one thing, Peter: that no one will come looking in time. A lawyer changes that. It's much harder to disappear someone who has legal representation. An attorney knows the person's name and where they're being held, and has the standing to go before a federal judge. **A habeas petition forces the government to justify why it's holding someone.** While the case is heard, an attorney can ask the court for an emergency stay to stop a deportation. Freedom Advocates grew out of the relationships The Workers Circle built at the 47 consecutive weeks of freedom vigils outside Alligator Alcatraz that shut down that detention camp permanently. Now, with immigration attorneys working at greatly reduced rates, we're reaching people in ICE detention centers across the country who have final orders, no lawyer, and no money. **None of us can stop ICE's machine alone.** But our two organizations and thousands of people giving together can put three attorneys in front of three people this week. That's three people ICE can no longer quietly erase. [**Will you split a gift of $10, $25, $50, or whatever feels meaningful to you between OnePA and The Workers Circle to help us raise $15,000 and file all three habeas cases this week?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqu-wUwIZ511oDywi-RcGpMm0-1_75ztOiSo5PpJdSF8Z5Kb-6fs30gmYH5gI0YIbNCH10LEeNJ8Yzquiqj6ZsOIMjkIVv-mb7aIQLfsHiTW48HO5KWGr1qK8Nns2LhAr6pa_XqURRis-R2qFXY8G31RSwM_l3lNJdjIJyTW9n7LEHz7Q8KDbJYxOW0UsxcxZ9XyFd2wybmJ1d9-Gxmvkmk0c25C4TrMVG0bklxW_XgY2fhRFdw7Qgjy7wlIoK6BZzslpBtX_DPLYWi3c-e2H-ixb6C6qtRKW0nJIEkkESAjFQ/4ur/HSL1z9JMQrGdf_3d7U_lmQ/h1/h001.DiQc7Hd7CtksmimjB6UNoT3kiXF8UAjidTMSv2d_4JM) _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately, split evenly between The Workers Circle and One Pennsylvania:_ | | | [Chip in $25 now](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqu-wUwIZ511oDywi-RcGpMm0-1_75ztOiSo5PpJdSF8Z5jAxLvjXPLIRRyuKvrOY7_oKab0HLaEmZKv6LK28InEBUcJbbG0dEU_d0-A_VDuUfqNB3s4IPpnsJWgilgogUQgBPzEExYSvkOqTFMbA76uBB3x3aUd0--IsXDwcoro-iyCEqxSkGf06VcKh6WjqItRAeaOl7-v1Ceeqokg9mYNSMyIVZoplJDqlcq3dzztBj2stp4o9wNL7kWLYZCgVihF0TXOdhRMJ5-tsiQqtQ9Yb0_RZsU9Y8FaCHdMf6WaQwsr1EXhQSv6OmLD9zVwBB-J9IOuJ9euipuJUOokM8_VPpGyu3jFKu1b-hwfNr_aQg/4ur/HSL1z9JMQrGdf_3d7U_lmQ/h2/h001.JqCv97R4CXBk_JjLthgzQnc9TLmubXnnneyjGBM9tM8)

clean_body: | | Peter, three people with strong habeas cases are sitting in ICE detention right now, and every hour we wait is another chance for them to disappear... Here's the situation: All three are facing deportation. None of them has a lawyer. If ICE moves them to another facility or puts them on a deportation flight before an attorney can file a habeas claim on their behalf, their families may not even know where they've gone. That's why OnePA is joining forces with The Workers Circle this week. Together, we need to raise $15,000 immediately to get all three attorneys who will file habeas cases. Last month, with no announcement, ICE quietly stopped listing people with final deportation orders in its online detainee locator. That's the database families and lawyers rely on to find someone in custody. More than 16,000 people in ICE detention are now missing from it. Lawyers search for their clients and come up empty. Families call facility after facility. Meanwhile, ICE moves people from one detention center to another, and deports people, often with no warning at all.Immigration lawyers say that for someone with a final order, even a few hours can make the difference between being deported and getting a judge to step in. This is serious enough that last week, human rights groups asked the United Nations panel that investigates enforced disappearances to intervene. DHS insists it isn't disappearing anyone. But when the government hides where it's holding people and rushes to deport them before anyone can find them, what else would you call it? ICE is counting on one thing, Peter: that no one will come looking in time. A lawyer changes that. It's much harder to disappear someone who has legal representation. An attorney knows the person's name and where they're being held, and has the standing to go before a federal judge. A habeas petition forces the government to justify why it's holding someone. While the case is heard, an attorney can ask the court for an emergency stay to stop a deportation. Freedom Advocates grew out of the relationships The Workers Circle built at the 47 consecutive weeks of freedom vigils outside Alligator Alcatraz that shut down that detention camp permanently. Now, with immigration attorneys working at greatly reduced rates, we're reaching people in ICE detention centers across the country who have final orders, no lawyer, and no money. None of us can stop ICE's machine alone. But our two organizations and thousands of people giving together can put three attorneys in front of three people this week. That's three people ICE can no longer quietly erase. Friend, Congress passed a budget. Congress decided how much would go to scientific research. Then the White House simply took $1.4 billion of it and redirected it elsewhere. That's what's happening at the National Science Foundation right now. After a White House directive this summer, about one-fifth of the agency's primary research budget is being shifted away from the basic science Congress mandated and toward the administration's chosen priorities, _**including artificial intelligence. **_ Let's call this what it is: corruption. As an NSF-funded scientist who worked at the U.S. Government Accountability Office, I will stand up to this kind of corruption to make sure our taxpayer dollars are used wisely and effectively instead of in the pockets of billionaires. Peter, Roy Cooper here. I’m worried.
We’re coming up on our final FEC deadline before Election Day, and unfortunately, we’re not where we need to be to reach our goal. [**_If you’re able to chip in today for the first time to help us get back on track, it would make a big impact and mean a lot to me._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1636&amount=5&t=9&akid=4381%2E124072%2E1dd8YI)
Here’s why we’re trying to raise $3 million (I know – it’s ambitious) before Wednesday:
North Carolina is where the fight for U.S. Senate control will be won or lost. Flipping this seat is a _must_ if we’re going to take back the majority, and that’s why the GOP is going all in to defeat me.
Republican super PACs have flooded this race with tens of millions to crush our momentum. President Trump has smeared my name to his millions of followers on social media. His buddy Stephen Miller even went on Fox News to rant and rave about me.
**If folks like you chip in and we hit our $3 million goal, we’ll be able to keep up with the GOP and ensure this race stays competitive. If we don’t meet this goal, we won’t.**
[**_That’s why this is so important, Peter, so I have to ask: Will you give $5 or whatever amount you can spare today to help us reach our goal, flip North Carolina and take back the Senate majority?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1636&amount=5&t=10&akid=4381%2E124072%2E1dd8YI)

**Dear Flyover Reader,** You come to _The Flyover_ for the news without the spin. On Monday, we're bringing that same approach to your money with **Flyover Finance** , our new free email edition. Here's the problem we're solving. The market moves in a hundred places at once--equities, rates, housing, labor data, the Fed, earnings. Most financial coverage either drowns you in noise or talks past you entirely. What's missing is the signal: what actually changed, why it matters, and what it means for your portfolio, your mortgage, and your retirement. _Flyover Finance_ is built to deliver that. In a five-minute read, we'll tell you what moved, why it moved, and what to watch next--with the context an informed reader expects and none of the jargon that gets in the way. name: Eric Pratt
subject: The truth about Matt Little’s radical platform
body:
Beyond the social media ads, here is what my opponent actually stands for.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/G5Ocw1tkvrb?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)
| | | | | | ,

As we get closer to Election Day, my opponent, Matt Little, is doing everything he can to hide his true record behind polished online videos. But voters in Minnesota's Second District deserve to know the unvarnished truth about the platform he is bringing to our communities.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/E7y9Xnw5lyg?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)
| | | | | | | | | | | |

When you look past the PR campaign, Matt Little’s agenda aligns directly with the most radical elements in Washington:
* **Attacking Local Law Enforcement:** Little publicly referred to federal law enforcement agents in Minnesota as "lawless street gangs" and officially pledged to slash federal immigration enforcement funding.

* **Government-Run Healthcare:** Instead of lowering prescription costs or protecting private plans, Little is championing full "Medicare for All"—a government takeover that would eliminate private health coverage for thousands of local families.

* **Reckless D.C. Spending:** Little supports massive tax increases on working families and new federal mandates that drive up the cost of groceries, gas, and energy.

Our community doesn't need extreme D.C. agendas or reckless policy experiments.I spent 30 years in the private sector stopping financial fraud and balancing budgets, and I am running to bring practical, common-sense solutions to Congress.
---
| [STAND WITH ME TO PROTECT MINNESOTA’S FUTURE >>](https://us.list-manage.com/jNwinYdR2c_?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)

Being an American with a conscience in 2026 requires something a little uncomfortable.: you have to decide whether you actually _**believe**_ any of this stuff.
"Liberty and justice for all." Do you believe that? Not, 'wouldn't it be nice?' Not, 'generally speaking, with a few reasonable exceptions.' For ALL.
Because if you believe it, then at some point it stops being a slogan and becomes an obligation.
And I think that's where we are.
I've been thinking a lot about what patriotism means when your government is doing things you cannot morally defend.
When people are being disappeared into indefinite detention, when our politics is increasingly indistinguishable from authoritarianism, when our money pays for bombs overseas while people sleep under bridges at home, when the richest country on Earth somehow keeps finding new ways to tell hardworking people there just isn't enough to go around.
What does it mean to love your country then?
I don't think it means pretending, and I don't think it means leaving the principles behind just because the institutions betrayed them.
**I think it means taking the principles more seriously than the institutions do.**
America taught us some very dangerous ideas: that people have intrinsic rights, that government gets its legitimacy from us, that power is supposed to answer to the people it affects, that nobody is supposed to be above the law, that liberty and justice belong to everyone.
Those ideas are dangerous because once people really believe them, we start noticing things.
We notice that "for all" cannot coexist peacefully with our current racial caste system, and _you know exactly what I'm talking about_.
That liberty means something for an immigrant in handcuffs too, that justice has to reach the poor person standing in court without a lawyer, that indigenous sovereignty and human dignity doesn't disappear just because acknowledging it is uncomfortable, that women should not have to organize our entire lives around the possibility of men's violence, that a country cannot call itself free while selling whole generations into debt for basic housing, healthcare, and education, that endless war is not normal or inevitable, that poverty is not a law of nature, that obedience is not citizenship, and that privacy is a human right, and our location, our data, our communications, our friendships are actually not for sale and are actually not the business of the government.
And once people notice those things, the systems of power start to feel a little exposed, a little threatened. **They don't like that.**
They'd rather keep us in the dark, keep the hierarchies and threats of violence firmly in place, and keep milking ordinary people in this country for every last dollar, hoping we don't notice.
_**Are you okay with that?**_
And no, America has never fully lived up to its own promise.
Our founders began with slavery written into the very Constitution. We made treaties, then broke them and settled on stolen land. We excluded women from political power. We built fortunes on exploited labor. We have overthrown governments, backed dictators, segregated neighborhoods, deported millions, run concentration camps and black sites, crushed unions, bombed civilians, and then taught a very tidy version of ourselves in school.
That history is **very real** , but something else is real, too.
Generation after generation, ordinary people looked at the words America claimed to believe, America taught us, and said, "All right, then prove it."
You say all men are created equal? Fine, then abolish slavery.
You say government belongs to the people? Fine, then women vote, too.
You say equal protection? Fine, then dismantle segregation.
You say liberty and justice for all? Fine, then it applies to Black people, immigrants, Muslims, queer people, prisoners, dissidents, poor people, and everybody else whose freedom and justice becomes inconvenient for some.
That fight is American, too. **Maybe more American than anything else we've ever done.**
The country makes a promise, power violates it, and ordinary people push back.
And our struggle, continual generational struggle, we force the promise to come closer to reality again and again and again.
**That's the patriotism I want.**
Not blind loyalty to the state, God, no. Loyalty to the _**Principle**_.
Because governments fail, parties fail, leaders fail, institutions get captured, constitutions get ignored, but _that doesn't have to be the end of America._
Because the question remains: **what are you going to do with the promises of the American Republic?**
I don't just mean voting every two years. Voting matters, of course it does, but citizenship was never supposed to mean hiring politicians to do democracy for us.
It means knowing your neighbors, showing up when somebody is being targeted, serving on juries, running for something, organizing your workplace, learning who controls your city budget, teaching your children the real history, supporting people who are building alternatives and becoming one of them, refusing propaganda even when it flatters your own side, refusing to become cruel just because cruelty has become fashionable, and: building things.
That part matters. A lot of us have become very good at describing what's broken, but society can't live inside a critique.
People need somewhere to go, food systems that feed them, housing they can afford, communities that know their names, ways to solve problems together, institutions worth trusting, a politics that gives people dignity and agency instead of turning us into terrified little voting blocks.
That is very much the work, and nobody is coming to do it for us.
**We are in our own hands. We are in each other's hands.**
There is no president who can save a population that has forgotten how to govern and care for itself, ourselves. No party can substitute for civic courage. No viral post can build a functioning community, and no elected official can permanently protect rights that people themselves, ourselves, have stopped defending.
So when I say I love this country, I don't mean I approve of everything it does. God, no.
I mean I am willing, **I am willing to take its best promises seriously,** more seriously than the people currently violating them.
Liberty and justice for all.
Government of, by, and for the people.
Equal protection under law.
Lifting our lamp beside the golden door.
Life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.
They're not decorations. These are instructions, commandments maybe.
And maybe **the most patriotic thing an American can do right now** is to stop asking whether America has earned our faith and start asking what we are willing to do to make those words true.
Not someday, not when the right person wins.
Us, now, here, together.
That's the job.
That's what it means to be an American.

clean_body: Watch now (8 mins) | And, what does it take to reclaim that identity proudly and courageously, and use it for good? | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? | | And, what does it take to reclaim that identity proudly and courageously, and use it for good? | | | Oct 10 | | | | | | | | | | | | Being an American with a conscience in 2026 requires something a little uncomfortable.: you have to decide whether you actually believe any of this stuff. "Liberty and justice for all." Do you believe that? Not, 'wouldn't it be nice?' Not, 'generally speaking, with a few reasonable exceptions.' For ALL. Because if you believe it, then at some point it stops being a slogan and becomes an obligation. And I think that's where we are. I've been thinking a lot about what patriotism means when your government is doing things you cannot morally defend. When people are being disappeared into indefinite detention, when our politics is increasingly indistinguishable from authoritarianism, when our money pays for bombs overseas while people sleep under bridges at home, when the richest country on Earth somehow keeps finding new ways to tell hardworking people there just isn't enough to go around. What does it mean to love your country then? I don't think it means pretending, and I don't think it means leaving the principles behind just because the institutions betrayed them. I think it means taking the principles more seriously than the institutions do. America taught us some very dangerous ideas: that people have intrinsic rights, that government gets its legitimacy from us, that power is supposed to answer to the people it affects, that nobody is supposed to be above the law, that liberty and justice belong to everyone. Those ideas are dangerous because once people really believe them, we start noticing things. We notice that "for all" cannot coexist peacefully with our current racial caste system, and you know exactly what I'm talking about. That liberty means something for an immigrant in handcuffs too, that justice has to reach the poor person standing in court without a lawyer, that indigenous sovereignty and human dignity doesn't disappear just because acknowledging it is uncomfortable, that women should not have to organize our entire lives around the possibility of men's violence, that a country cannot call itself free while selling whole generations into debt for basic housing, healthcare, and education, that endless war is not normal or inevitable, that poverty is not a law of nature, that obedience is not citizenship, and that privacy is a human right, and our location, our data, our communications, our friendships are actually not for sale and are actually not the business of the government. And once people notice those things, the systems of power start to feel a little exposed, a little threatened. They don't like that. They'd rather keep us in the dark, keep the hierarchies and threats of violence firmly in place, and keep milking ordinary people in this country for every last dollar, hoping we don't notice. Are you okay with that? And no, America has never fully lived up to its own promise. Our founders began with slavery written into the very Constitution. We made treaties, then broke them and settled on stolen land. We excluded women from political power. We built fortunes on exploited labor. We have overthrown governments, backed dictators, segregated neighborhoods, deported millions, run concentration camps and black sites, crushed unions, bombed civilians, and then taught a very tidy version of ourselves in school. That history is very real , but something else is real, too. Generation after generation, ordinary people looked at the words America claimed to believe, America taught us, and said, "All right, then prove it." You say all men are created equal? Fine, then abolish slavery. You say government belongs to the people? Fine, then women vote, too. You say equal protection? Fine, then dismantle segregation. You say liberty and justice for all? Fine, then it applies to Black people, immigrants, Muslims, queer people, prisoners, dissidents, poor people, and everybody else whose freedom and justice becomes inconvenient for some. That fight is American, too. Maybe more American than anything else we've ever done. The country makes a promise, power violates it, and ordinary people push back. And our struggle, continual generational struggle, we force the promise to come closer to reality again and again and again. That's the patriotism I want. Not blind loyalty to the state, God, no. Loyalty to the Principle. Because governments fail, parties fail, leaders fail, institutions get captured, constitutions get ignored, but that doesn't have to be the end of America. Because the question remains: what are you going to do with the promises of the American Republic? I don't just mean voting every two years. Voting matters, of course it does, but citizenship was never supposed to mean hiring politicians to do democracy for us. It means knowing your neighbors, showing up when somebody is being targeted, serving on juries, running for something, organizing your workplace, learning who controls your city budget, teaching your children the real history, supporting people who are building alternatives and becoming one of them, refusing propaganda even when it flatters your own side, refusing to become cruel just because cruelty has become fashionable, and: building things. That part matters. A lot of us have become very good at describing what's broken, but society can't live inside a critique. People need somewhere to go, food systems that feed them, housing they can afford, communities that know their names, ways to solve problems together, institutions worth trusting, a politics that gives people dignity and agency instead of turning us into terrified little voting blocks. That is very much the work, and nobody is coming to do it for us. We are in our own hands. We are in each other's hands. There is no president who can save a population that has forgotten how to govern and care for itself, ourselves. No party can substitute for civic courage. No viral post can build a functioning community, and no elected official can permanently protect rights that people themselves, ourselves, have stopped defending. So when I say I love this country, I don't mean I approve of everything it does. God, no. I mean I am willing, I am willing to take its best promises seriously, more seriously than the people currently violating them. Liberty and justice for all. Government of, by, and for the people. Equal protection under law. Lifting our lamp beside the golden door. Life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. They're not decorations. These are instructions, commandments maybe. And maybe the most patriotic thing an American can do right now is to stop asking whether America has earned our faith and start asking what we are willing to do to make those words true. Not someday, not when the right person wins. Us, now, here, together. That's the job. That's what it means to be an American. | | ---|---|--- You 're currently a free subscriber to "It's a Matter of Integrity" by Melissa Chaudhry. [ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
We want to be clear about something: John James knows he’s
losing.

He’s seen the polls, heard from Michiganders fed up with the failed
leadership in Washington, and most importantly, he’s watched our momentum
build one conversation at a time.

He’s scared he’s going to lose, and now, he’s desperately trying to
rebrand weeks before Election Day.

First, John James called for a “quick end” to a war he voted for six
times.

Then, he scrubbed mentions of Donald Trump from his campaign website.

Next, he got on the debate stage and claimed to be “too left” for
Republicans.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/20897?t=1001&akid=1979%2E181023%2Ec28bLz ]This isn’t just a case of changing strategy. This is a desperate attempt
to deceive voters and lie about his agenda. John James can try to distance
himself from Trump now, but make no mistake: he’s spent years
rubber-stamping every single one of Trump’s dangerous schemes. We can’t
allow John James to confuse the record and lie to voters. Will you pitch
in today to help us fight back before our opponent redefines this race?

At least $9 billion in fraud and stolen taxpayer money, rising crime, and failing schools.
They are going 100 miles per hour in the wrong direction.
Peggy Flanagan, a failed career politician who enabled the policies that got us here. Her way doesn't work. And yet we've been paying Peggy Flanagan with our hard-earned money for 20 years.

We can't let all the rampant, unprecedented fraud that took place under her watch go unnoticed. It's a national disgrace. That's why Tim Walz was forced to end his re-election campaign... Meanwhile, his right hand wants to be our next U.S. Senator.
She's cut from the same cloth as every other Socialist pretending to be moderate today.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: New York Times: Greg Abbott trailing
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
The New York Times last polled our race 3 months ago and found us down 7. This poll has swung 10 points since then.
Friend, look at this:
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_mcbride_20261010-2.DlNDz8&refcode=em20261010-3961&amount=5&t=1&akid=3961%2E21716%2E_Lvy-Z)
In June, the _New York Times_ /Siena poll had me trailing Greg Abbott by 7 points, 51% to 44%.
**Now, that same poll has me ahead, 49% to 46%.**
That's a 10-point swing in three months, from one of the most respected pollsters in the country. It's not a fluke, either. This is the third poll showing us ahead of Abbott, and it's the most recent one, taken after weeks of Abbott's attack ads flooding Texas airwaves. **[Split $5 right now between Congresswoman Sarah McBride and my campaign to help us turn this polling lead into a win](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_mcbride_20261010-2.DlNDz8&refcode=em20261010-3961&amount=5&t=2&akid=3961%2E21716%2E_Lvy-Z).**
The _New York Times_ also ran a major story on the state of play in Texas. Read this:
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_mcbride_20261010-2.DlNDz8&refcode=em20261010-3961&amount=5&t=3&akid=3961%2E21716%2E_Lvy-Z)
**Ten-to-one. Abbott has thrown everything he has at this race, and he still can't put it away.**
Wendy Davis put it this way in the same article: "People have vastly underestimated Gina. Dollar for dollar, she's running the best statewide campaign we've ever seen."
That's what grassroots supporters like you have built $5 and $10 at a time. We haven't come close to matching Abbott's money, but every dollar has gone further than anyone thought it could. [**Will you split a contribution today between Sarah McBride and my campaign to help us keep our momentum going in the final stretch?**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_mcbride_20261010-2.DlNDz8&refcode=em20261010-3961&amount=5&t=4&akid=3961%2E21716%2E_Lvy-Z)
The Times was also honest about what still stands in our way. Texas has 20 separate media markets, and national donors routinely pass the state over because reaching all of them is so expensive. And one in five Texas voters still doesn't know who I am.
Here's what the last three months have taught us: the more Texans get to know me, the more this race moves. **Every one of those voters is someone we can reach, but only if we have the resources to do it.** Abbott has raised more than $106 million in this race, and he's going to keep spending it in the final month to drag this race back his way.
We are 24 days from Election Day. The polls tell us this race can be won. What happens next depends on whether we have the financial resources to communicate our message to the voters who need to hear it.
[**Can you split $5 right now between Sarah McBride and my campaign to help us reach every voter in every corner of Texas and defeat Greg Abbott on November 3rd?**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_mcbride_20261010-2.DlNDz8&refcode=em20261010-3961&amount=5&t=5&akid=3961%2E21716%2E_Lvy-Z)
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_mcbride_20261010-2.DlNDz8&amount=5&refcode=em20261010-3961&t=24&akid=3961%2E21716%2E_Lvy-Z)**
For 32 years, Texans have been told a Democrat can't win statewide. A 10-point swing after more than $70 million in spending against us says otherwise. Let's go take Texas back.
Thank you — for everything,
Gina

That's a 10-point swing in three months, from one of the most respected pollsters in the country. It's not a fluke, either. This is the third poll showing us ahead of Abbott, and it's the most recent one, taken after weeks of Abbott's attack ads flooding Texas airwaves. . The New York Times also ran a major story on the state of play in Texas. Read this: Ten-to-one. Abbott has thrown everything he has at this race, and he still can't put it away. Wendy Davis put it this way in the same article: "People have vastly underestimated Gina. Dollar for dollar, she's running the best statewide campaign we've ever seen." That's what grassroots supporters like you have built $5 and $10 at a time. We haven't come close to matching Abbott's money, but every dollar has gone further than anyone thought it could. The Times was also honest about what still stands in our way. Texas has 20 separate media markets, and national donors routinely pass the state over because reaching all of them is so expensive. And one in five Texas voters still doesn't know who I am. Here's what the last three months have taught us: the more Texans get to know me, the more this race moves. Every one of those voters is someone we can reach, but only if we have the resources to do it. Abbott has raised more than $106 million in this race, and he's going to keep spending it in the final month to drag this race back his way. We are 24 days from Election Day. The polls tell us this race can be won. What happens next depends on whether we have the financial resources to communicate our message to the voters who need to hear it. For 32 years, Texans have been told a Democrat can't win statewide. A 10-point swing after more than $70 million in spending against us says otherwise. Let's go take Texas back. Thank you — for everything, Gina

| | | The Trump administration is dismantling one of the world's most important science laboratories.

clean_body: To win the game... | | | | Friend, The latest odds show the Senate Majority is a 50-50 toss-up. That’s roughly the same odds as a football team scoring a touchdown when facing a fourth and goal at the two-yard line. So think of it this way... With absolutely no margin for error, our play call needs to be perfect. To win the midterms, we need to surpass the Democrats in total voter verifications during the final, critical weeks of the elections. At the end of the day, the ONLY thing that matters is locking in verified votes! Trust me, I know a thing or two about standing on the sidelines. I spent 30 years as a sideline reporter for football on Sunday nights. But I couldn't stand there and do nothing while the Radical Left destroyed our country, so I got off the sidelines to run for Senate in Minnesota. Now, I’m asking YOU to get off the sidelines as well by verifying your voter profile. Friend,

Okay, let’s dive in head-first: **Public campaign financing.**
It’s not a policy you hear about very often in the news, or on the campaign trail for that matter.
**But it’s a game-changer for our elections. And here in Baltimore County, we know it better than anyone.**
Here’s what makes our elections different:
If you’re running for Baltimore County Council, the county will match up to $80,000 worth of donations, with the following conditions:
* You’ve raised at least $15,000 and 150 qualifying donations from _residents of Baltimore County._ _No, out-of-state donations don’t count._

* You can’t give more than $250 to your own campaign. _Nope, no matching funds for millionaire self-funders._

* **You can’t accept a dime from PACs, super PACs, or corporations.**

Pretty simple, right? If you want to run for office in Baltimore County, you don’t need a Rolodex of megadonors and super PACs to get your campaign off the ground. Thanks to public campaign financing, regular people have a real shot at winning — no corporate money required.
**We’ve already seen the benefits here in Baltimore County. Now, I want to take it nationwide.**
Not another 200-page bill that sounds impressive and changes absolutely nothing. _A real change to who gets to participate in our democracy._
The status quo we all despise right now? It’s a choice. It’s a deliberate decision made by politicians and their corporate donors. The system is clearly working for _them_ — tax handouts to the one percent, corrupt stock trades among members of Congress — so why bother changing anything?
But before I can work on changing the system in Washington, I need to make sure I’m still there.
**We have just weeks until Election Day, and our campaign is fighting to reach every voter we can.**

clean_body: You don’t need a Rolodex of megadonors and super PACs to get your campaign off the ground = Fair warning: This email is going to be long, thorough, and... honestly? Pretty nerdy. = | | = Okay, let’s dive in head-first: Public campaign financing. It’s not a policy you hear about very often in the news, or on the campaign trail for that matter. But it’s a game-changer for our elections. And here in Baltimore County, we know it better than anyone. Here’s what makes our elections different: If you’re running for Baltimore County Council, the county will match up to $80,000 worth of donations, with the following conditions: You’ve raised at least $15,000 and 150 qualifying donations from residents of Baltimore County. No, out-of-state donations don’t count. You can’t give more than $250 to your own campaign. Nope, no matching funds for millionaire self-funders. You can’t accept a dime from PACs, super PACs, or corporations. Pretty simple, right? If you want to run for office in Baltimore County, you don’t need a Rolodex of megadonors and super PACs to get your campaign off the ground. Thanks to public campaign financing, regular people have a real shot at winning — no corporate money required. We’ve already seen the benefits here in Baltimore County. Now, I want to take it nationwide. Not another 200-page bill that sounds impressive and changes absolutely nothing. A real change to who gets to participate in our democracy. The status quo we all despise right now? It’s a choice. It’s a deliberate decision made by politicians and their corporate donors. The system is clearly working for them — tax handouts to the one percent, corrupt stock trades among members of Congress — so why bother changing anything? But before I can work on changing the system in Washington, I need to make sure I’m still there. body:
The good news: we are winning the money race in the Governor's race. The honest news: the Senate race is a different story. |
---
Peter,

_**[Here is something you might not have heard about Florida lately.....](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=d7802890536f400eb58c182fe941f702&_e=g69SeDMt660yizXlGg_vB6hHveMOaksjCXxXnJE7P3AxBnWvja8TwgRoG7xybaPYLPXr61A5o5RYV0bPvYLk3MANfhnXAU2Stq2SX976r9YemEnupNvAcd9xT-gNfMDNnX_nwIf_T7huXXVqHbgX_denBMdDZYEdKnZnCNVJIvl3AWQEHlpvTVQ5DjWbjfOny3Tvl-u2UajfI0lUkLcwlwmoYSIs_IXgUNpp-qZA0bJwBCDg83oErf9sIMHYKTzmXdH9H6OsX7v7TE0JpCfk556Ilp0sE7CT1gUum5R26Kqjgw-YzsQ7H-ydnzo0fmQ1lnbtoK93xZaEmenNuTZSCJSWNKQIDzjRYINzmzZ8yiARnr6lL0FxbSa_jMj2PihGgCy_PBIw6pwfquJ31MxzgA%3D%3D)**_

Republican Byron Donalds has outraised Democrat David Jolly by more than 10 to 1 in the Governor's race. Donalds has raised nearly $10.2 million. Jolly has raised roughly $1 million. In a state as large and as expensive to advertise in as Florida, that kind of financial advantage is significant. It means more ads, more ground game, more voter contact, and more of the infrastructure that wins races in October.

[
[**FUEL THE FIGHT >>**](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=d7802890536f400eb58c182fe941f702&_e=g69SeDMt660yizXlGg_vB6hHveMOaksjCXxXnJE7P3AxBnWvja8TwgRoG7xybaPYLPXr61A5o5RYV0bPvYLk3MANfhnXAU2Stq2SX976r9YemEnupNvAcd9xT-gNfMDNnX_nwIf_T7huXXVqHbgX_denBMdDZYEdKnZnCNVJIvl3AWQEHlpvTVQ5DjWbjfOny3Tvl-u2UajfI0lUkLcwlwmoYSIs_IXgUNpp-qZA0bJwBCDg83oErf9sIMHYKTzmvfC02_l18HQykPIttqFMzra0VxdIBssppPKPf_woxOMvl45unFNpP4ANgMRWjOeBTVhYmk8Jc2PwxxctXzNUGFl6mxvolV6yd9wKBgGPAMr4FegoEQm_SFUL0OQzF-AvYKWECgyxO7Y1QeYkZdNjeQ%3D%3D) ](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=d7802890536f400eb58c182fe941f702&_e=g69SeDMt660yizXlGg_vB6hHveMOaksjCXxXnJE7P3AxBnWvja8TwgRoG7xybaPYLPXr61A5o5RYV0bPvYLk3MANfhnXAU2Stq2SX976r9YemEnupNvAcd9xT-gNfMDNnX_nwIf_T7huXXVqHbgX_denBMdDZYEdKnZnCNVJIvl3AWQEHlpvTVQ5DjWbjfOny3Tvl-u2UajfI0lUkLcwlwmoYSIs_IXgUNpp-qZA0bJwBCDg83oErf9sIMHYKTzmIaLBKY26U_zg8G5QS5DqJO6jalqfKMgJh1YMB2R2noMcWLoY5Glq832wB04xCtQvwQ_m_7MznL1dvglpmSC-XdmQADluQ8JRl36FPG61h3hioOTs--bpUu-tzIgbf-Fva06PQOxCe1Eg17viZ3rlPA%3D%3D)
That is genuinely good news. And we do not say that enough.

Nationally, Democratic Senate candidates are outraising Republicans in seven GOP-held Senate seats. **[Florida is on that list.](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=d7802890536f400eb58c182fe941f702&_e=g69SeDMt660yizXlGg_vB6hHveMOaksjCXxXnJE7P3AxBnWvja8TwgRoG7xybaPYLPXr61A5o5RYV0bPvYLk3MANfhnXAU2Stq2SX976r9YemEnupNvAcd9xT-gNfMDNnX_nwIf_T7huXXVqHbgX_denBMdDZYEdKnZnCNVJIvl3AWQEHlpvTVQ5DjWbjfOny3Tvl-u2UajfI0lUkLcwlwmoYSIs_IXgUNpp-qZA0bJwBCDg83oErf9sIMHYKTzmZco56PeufRLn_f2d-d6mAIhs3v7Te6PrAH4zbrHugbFg-JwfyJyRMQ81h9KQ8sOdteQ8rL3VuxgdOWmuOMy-BduuIR9BAockxzjC5st48hm0fD3qTvCxOcZFJKtBpAKB6QWOjBUsrz-LCDMrDB902w%3D%3D)** The same national liberal donor network that has been targeting this state all cycle is still writing checks because flipping a Senate seat in President Trump's home state would be the biggest symbolic victory the Left could claim in 2026.

[**HELP US FUEL THE FIGHT >>**](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=d7802890536f400eb58c182fe941f702&_e=g69SeDMt660yizXlGg_vB6hHveMOaksjCXxXnJE7P3AxBnWvja8TwgRoG7xybaPYLPXr61A5o5RYV0bPvYLk3MANfhnXAU2Stq2SX976r9YemEnupNvAcd9xT-gNfMDNnX_nwIf_T7huXXVqHbgX_denBMdDZYEdKnZnCNVJIvl3AWQEHlpvTVQ5DjWbjfOny3Tvl-u2UajfI0lUkLcwlwmoYSIs_IXgUNpp-qZA0bJwBCDg83oErf9sIMHYKTzm_Ptb1Qqlfe4UxQ7uikUGPOgFs_spUxHuVilAFenMLsJNp2OqvgjQJEGAdtPn6aSv1Qg0ds4RcNrY3B_caC4KEMFi27BxE4FgMnjKaWDXiVnU9MeDTKTEWcEUbgazJXVx_ch2vCu3TNIm2t95uCjfUw%3D%3D)
[**The Senate race needs fuel.**](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=d7802890536f400eb58c182fe941f702&_e=g69SeDMt660yizXlGg_vB6hHveMOaksjCXxXnJE7P3AxBnWvja8TwgRoG7xybaPYLPXr61A5o5RYV0bPvYLk3MANfhnXAU2Stq2SX976r9YemEnupNvAcd9xT-gNfMDNnX_nwIf_T7huXXVqHbgX_denBMdDZYEdKnZnCNVJIvl3AWQEHlpvTVQ5DjWbjfOny3Tvl-u2UajfI0lUkLcwlwmoYSIs_IXgUNpp-qZA0bJwBCDg83oErf9sIMHYKTzmWDngOrp52WZPhWOumb3JiS0AsSuom7QU8EPK683MvfjBQXY4jFp_aKjnbNVQcyz6RGP6zZ3o2B6RthxDqTFFPj-P9SR0ANHT-PWkNHVyqUnk34CKQtmwwSPaj1fvA34iKlrlPeLRc9RUqmI0Qe_HPQ%3D%3D) And in a state with multiple expensive media markets, a ground game that has to cover millions of voters, and an election that will be decided in the final weeks of October, running low on resources in the home stretch is not a risk we can afford to take.

[Every dollar raised in September goes directly into October, which is the month that decides everything.](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=d7802890536f400eb58c182fe941f702&_e=g69SeDMt660yizXlGg_vB6hHveMOaksjCXxXnJE7P3AxBnWvja8TwgRoG7xybaPYLPXr61A5o5RYV0bPvYLk3MANfhnXAU2Stq2SX976r9YemEnupNvAcd9xT-gNfMDNnX_nwIf_T7huXXVqHbgX_denBMdDZYEdKnZnCNVJIvl3AWQEHlpvTVQ5DjWbjfOny3Tvl-u2UajfI0lUkLcwlwmoYSIs_IXgUNpp-qZA0bJwBCDg83oErf9sIMHYKTzmq20mFhTNrP1Vhgb7l6FpSPbCOqG-OyWT5P0iQCueM90fVmEGvoOxrC9Dnf9Xrkcd0siCIrfjlNtD_-bqhAeMjYz7NUHC4CfCWoKsvq7Q0O6vIku3-JvMGJAkcgaWv4tfF7Y3lDYWzE8Gq_IlsvvH0g%3D%3D) The voter contact operations. The final ad buys. The ground game turnout programs that move the needle in the precincts where margins are razor thin.

Annie Andrews has Hollywood. I have you. |
Peter - more Hollywood donors are lining up for my opponent.

**Team:** Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections. Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office. **That's no longer the case.** Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a _regional processing facility_ , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts. **How does this impact vote-by-mail?** If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- _something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those_ \-- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, _a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day,_ making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control. **Of course, this was followed by the recent news that USPS won't deliver your ballot unless your state put your name on Trump's list** \-- usurping the Constitution and trying to take control of elections away from the states in order to suppress the vote. **[Team, Every voter needs to know about these massive changes. Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office. That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts. How does this impact vote-by-mail? Case File No DRT-ED-EYES · Special File · The Night Shift
The Robots Already Clocked In. The Next Fortune Is in What Lets Them See.
A humanoid robot worked 10-hour shifts at BMW’s South Carolina plant for 11 months and helped build more than 30,000 cars. Now the race is on to build them by the million, and every one needs a set of eyes.
Threat level 3/5 — Guarded
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
For years, humanoid robots were a trade-show act: a robot folds a shirt, waves at the crowd, and goes back in its box. That era ended quietly, in a body shop in Spartanburg, South Carolina, on the line that builds the BMW X3.
The evidence board
| | What Happened in Spartanburg
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the shift log.** Over an 11-month program, a Figure 02 humanoid loaded about 90,000 sheet-metal parts for welding, logged more than 1,250 hours of runtime and helped build more than 30,000 BMW X3s. By the tenth month it was working full 10-hour shifts.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the promotion.** In June 2026, BMW said the successor model, Figure 03, was starting work in Spartanburg on a harder job: sorting mixed parts into the exact order the assembly line needs them.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the scale-up.** In January, Tesla said it would end Model S and Model X production and convert that space at its Fremont factory into a robot line designed for up to 1 million humanoids a year.
The detail most people miss
| | Every Robot Needs Eyes
---|---
A humanoid can have perfect hands and a powerful AI brain, but if it can’t see what’s in front of it, it can’t do anything useful on a factory floor. Parts arrive in different positions. People walk past. Bins get moved. The robot has to see all of it, understand it and react in a fraction of a second.
| EVIDENCE
---
Figure says the cameras on its new robot run at about twice the frame rate of the previous model, with about a quarter of the delay and a 60% wider field of view. It added a camera in the palm of each hand so the robot can still see when its main cameras are blocked.
| EVIDENCE
---
In August, the CEO of one sensor maker said customers are putting as many as six to 12 cameras on each humanoid.
| OUR THEORY
---
Multiply 6 to 12 cameras, plus the chips that make sense of the images, by a factory line designed for a million robots a year. The companies that supply the vision layer don’t need to pick the winning robot. They get paid by all of them.
Decoder
| | The Number Wall Street Is Using
---|---
| | “13 million humanoids in service by 2035. More than 1 billion by 2050.”— Morgan Stanley’s humanoid robot forecast
---|---
What it says
Robots go from a few thousand prototypes to millions of workers within a decade.
What it means

[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek, if we were
sitting across a table somewhere instead of doing this over email, here's
what I'd tell you about where this race stands.

We're in decent shape. (I'm not going to pretend otherwise just because a
scarier version of this email would raise more money today.)

But "decent shape" in Pennsylvania has never meant much, given just how
fast the pendulum can swing.

Democrats swept every statewide race here in 2022. Republicans swept every
one in 2024. Donald Trump carried this Commonwealth two years ago. Leads
here come apart fast, and they come apart unexpectedly.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/16573?t=1001&akid=588%2E245147%2EETaG85 ]So what I'd actually ask you over that coffee is this: Will you pitch
in any amount today to help us make sure we leave nothing on the table on
November 3rd?

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/16573?t=1002&akid=588%2E245147%2EETaG85 ]Chip in →

Not because something is on fire. Because nothing is, and that's exactly
when campaigns get complacent.

What worries me isn't a collapse. It's a quiet few weeks where the money
slows, we trim an ad buy here and a canvass launch there, and nobody
notices until the margin comes in at half a point and everyone spends a
month asking what happened.

I've watched that happen to too many well-oiled machines,
Derek. But our campaign isn’t
going to be one of them.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/16573?t=1003&akid=588%2E245147%2EETaG85 ]So please: If you'd rather we win this race than spend November

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: I think about this a lot these days…
body:
I did what any mom would’ve done. I fought back.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
I want to tell you a story, Peter — one with me saying thank you.
Years ago, my son’s elementary school was marked for closure. They blamed budget cuts.
I wasn’t a politician. I was a mom who didn’t want her kid’s school to disappear. So I rallied the other parents, ran for a seat on the Austin School Board, _and won_.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261010_4_school.hk9Thp&refcode=em20261010-2398&amount=5&t=1&akid=2398%2E299639%2Ee8nhWK)
We didn’t just save my son’s school — _we kept every school in our district open_.
I think about that fight a lot these days. Because every single time I’ve been told something is impossible, it turned out that “impossible” just meant nobody had tried hard enough yet.

Friends, it's Mary Trump. Five years ago, after the attack on the Capitol, I said my uncle was unstable and needed to be removed from office immediately. _I was right then, and the case is only more clear now._ I've made this argument as a clinical psychologist, as his niece, and as someone who grew up watching exactly how my family wields power. My opinion as to whether Donald is capable of doing the job of the presidency has never wavered, and the evidence should be even more obvious to anyone willing to look. Consider what we've all watched recently. Donald calls foreign leaders by the wrong names. He invents countries that don't exist. He cannot stay awake through his own meetings. His hands are bruised, his ankles are swollen, and he has no impulse control. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141151977/652608588/974976698?refcode=em-10.10.26-all-2-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS84OTkxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNTRiMDY2YS1lOWM0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=w91rHL4DsP49d_hOniJEjUE8jC1llOpKgMXGwFOVv74=) **Here's the part I most need you to understand: Donald isn't a different person. His cognitive, psychological, and physical decline are simply revealing who he's always been.** Meanwhile, the people constitutionally empowered to act — his Cabinet, his party — are painfully aware of his unfitness even as they work to cover it up. They have decided that their own hold on power is worth more to them than the country's safety or the rights of the people they purport to serve. They will not act on their own. **So the responsibility falls to us, and the only real remedy available to us is an electoral one. **Cyndi Munson (OK)** : Cyndi has spent her career fighting for Oklahoma's working families. In this open race, we have the chance to elect a proven leader and take back power in a state where failed Republican policies have made everyday life harder and less affordable.

| | | | | For more than 50 years, something has been quietly eating away at the real-world value of the U.S. dollar.

Weiss Ratings calls it **“Project Pyramid.”**

It began in 1971, when Washington decoupled the dollar from gold.

Since then, the supply of U.S. dollars has exploded.

At the same time, the cost of housing, healthcare, education, energy and everyday life has climbed dramatically.

And according to Gavin Magor, a senior research analyst at Weiss Ratings, this isn’t some temporary problem that Washington can easily reverse.

America is carrying enormous levels of debt.

Foreign nations are reducing their dependence on the dollar.

And policymakers continue relying on the same monetary system that helped create the problem in the first place.

So what can ordinary investors do?

The answer isn’t simply to pile up more cash.

It’s to potentially grow your investment capital [faster than the dollar loses its real-world value.](https://links.dpt.deepregimetrends.com/u/click?_t=4a25883d9bf54436b571b8aa9717dcca&_m=a1feaec7ba3e4239ac5a4b282bd3d71a&_e=epEWKwXhUA8xqMtmFotjXarEUZpKUeZzRD5I0aFfw50ZiXf9S9vNTcORPbiZ_2TcEkIF7t9gKrmyj5gqiCh4xVqOTxUOw8lYen8qC_Ot5454gS4UJRMLpaN6Ux1bCm5RADAnAQcCrtL3f5HVI3jgOZMJY_nwfYbl6GjZFiXHwc-dv6gN2u3gz9Eo76TnNd9tQoJR6ZI87ymSQE_XeeoSuO74VijeQg2QCCE5a5K8mNugsv5XEQNEc2ZdVeQC39uh4B-yPooe_Y46nlsUAq6ne9uvZo_elAJ2zROpM6-jpNuGKhCR0xu7QfvDksL0xQBwhXG-rqU20mELMnyb-nLQE_t7QaT-JH1G5qncoRbeuBVdYCBxqlSOVidYTxxlOq_YDrcZiKht7Xem6kW4gg2xxIy6uQfV9zYFMpc19qTyhAKdIqTE_zwd58ruqEE_mSfTugv48kF6BfepbafTp2EcYkuwVusb2xpJPBkwhVLVbkRJnqHJdBpX8TtS2CDEEC8o8FIxAMoV9MnpCAP5mgHigSne9CWVSkY71AnzHhXK7qs%3D)
