Case File No DRT-ED-1971 · Special File · The Slow Leak
In 1971, One Decision Changed the Dollar. Fifty-Five Years Later, Your Savings Are Still Paying for It.
A dollar from 1971 now buys about what 12 cents did back then. The national debt just passed $40 trillion, and the dollar’s share of world reserves has fallen from 71% to 57%. The leak hasn’t stopped. It may be speeding up.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
On the evening of August 15, 1971, President Nixon went on television and cut the last link between the U.S. dollar and gold. It was sold to the public as a temporary measure. It was never reversed. Since then, Washington has been able to create dollars without anything physical standing behind them, and it has used that freedom generously.
Most people never feel this as a single event. They feel it as rent that keeps rising, groceries that cost more every year, and savings that seem to shrink while sitting still. That’s the point. A slow leak doesn’t set off alarms.
The evidence board
| | What 55 Years of Paper Money Did
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the dollar itself.** Based on consumer prices, $1 in 1971 has the same buying power as about $8.27 today. Put the other way, a 1971 dollar now buys roughly what 12 cents did then. Prices have risen about 727% in that time.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the debt.** On October 8, 2026, total U.S. public debt hit a record of about $40.3 trillion, according to Treasury data. Earlier this year, the portion held by the public passed the size of the entire U.S. economy for the first time since World War II.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the rest of the world.** The dollar made up about 71% of global central bank reserves around 2000. In the first quarter of 2026, it was 57%, according to the IMF. Meanwhile, gold traded around $4,169 an ounce on October 9.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit D — this year.** Consumer prices were up 3.4% over the 12 months to August. Gasoline alone was up 27.4%.
Decoder
| | The Line That Explains Everything
---|---
| | “The dollar is our currency, but it’s your problem.”— U.S. Treasury Secretary John Connally to European finance ministers, 1971
---|---
What it says
The U.S. can run its currency to suit itself, and others will have to adjust.
What it means
**Our theory:** the “others” were never just foreign governments. They include every American with money in a savings account or a fixed pension. When the dollar is managed to make government debt easier to carry, the cost lands on whoever holds dollars.
The mechanism
| | How the Leak Works
---|---
| | STEP 1
---
Debt grows
Washington spends more than it collects, year after year, and borrows the difference.
| | STEP 2
---
Money supply grows
Over time, more dollars enter the system to keep that borrowing manageable. More dollars chasing the same goods pushes prices up.
| | STEP 3
---
Savers pay
Each dollar buys a little less. Debt gets easier to carry in real terms. Cash quietly loses value, and most people never notice the moment it happens.
| OUR THEORY
---
Holding cash feels safe because the number on the statement never goes down. But the number isn’t what matters. What matters is what it buys. Over 55 years, cash has been one of the most reliable ways to lose purchasing power. The people who kept ahead did one thing differently: they owned assets that could grow faster than the dollar was losing value.
| ClassificationOngoing
---
None of this is new, and that’s exactly why it’s dangerous. The forces that have been eating the dollar since 1971 are still in place, and some are getting bigger: record debt, rising interest costs, and foreign buyers slowly stepping back. Waiting for the problem to fix itself has never worked.
Tripwires
| | What We’re Watching
---|---
| |
---
**October 14:** the September inflation report. Another month of fast-rising energy prices would keep pressure on household budgets.
| |
---
**The debt clock:** how quickly the total moves from $40 trillion toward $41 trillion.
| |
---
**Gold:** whether central banks keep adding to their holdings while trimming dollars.
| The riddle · answer at the end of the fileSince 1971, the dollar has lost close to 90% of its buying power. So why does it still look strong against most other currencies?
---
|
---
Riddle answer
**Because it’s being compared with currencies that are losing value too.** Exchange rates measure one paper currency against another. They don’t measure what your money buys. **Our theory:** the comparison that matters for your retirement isn’t dollars versus euros. It’s dollars versus the cost of living, and on that scoreboard, the dollar has been losing for 55 years.

Hi friend,
From the start of this campaign, I have thought about why I made the decision to run for the U.S. Senate in Kansas.
I'm a husband, a father of two remarkable daughters, and a grandfather. I'm also the founding pastor of the largest United Methodist Church in the United States and a proud fifth-generation Kansan.
My great-great grandparents moved to Dickinson County, Kansas, 147 years ago. They were farmers and builders and good people who helped build their communities of Hope and Elmo. Like them, I love Kansas and its people, and I love my country. **That 's why I feel called to run for the U.S. Senate.**
Today, our nation's highest values and aspirations are being undermined, and chaos and corruption in Washington is tearing Americans apart. We've insulted and alienated our allies. And we have a government in DC that's making life harder for Kansans. People can't afford the basics - food, gas and health care.
**I 'm running for the United States Senate because I care about our country, because things need to change, and because I know I can build bridges, bring people together to solve problems, and be a champion for Kansas.**
I've heard from Kansans all over the state who voted for Roger Marshall six years ago and now feel he's not listening to them. People who have met with him and often feel unseen or dismissed by the man they elected to represent them.
And now, this race has gotten close. Between political experts and polls, it's clear we have a real chance to win here in Kansas and get to work for families.
I believe we can and must do more - and as the leader of a large, diverse congregation of roughly equal parts Democrats, Republicans and Independents, I am ready to disrupt partisan gridlock in Washington, bring people together and create meaningful solutions to our problems.
**[That work starts](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1e99e072-86ab-420b-9f88-5dc193a16478?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** _**[now](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1e99e072-86ab-420b-9f88-5dc193a16478?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_**[, and if you agree that what's going on in our country is unacceptable, then I need you with me. Nothing about this race will be easy, and we're going to need an incredible grassroots team to create change in Kansas. Please consider joining us now by making a grassroots donation.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1e99e072-86ab-420b-9f88-5dc193a16478?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/1e99e072-86ab-420b-9f88-5dc193a16478?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
My team and I will be in touch soon with campaign updates, plans for the future, and more ways to get involved - because this really will take all of us.
Thank you - now let's bring some Kansas values to Washington.
Adam

[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Hi, I know you get a lot of emails from me. So I wanted to
take a step back and tell you a little bit more about me and why I’m
running to be the next Governor of Michigan.

Ever since I was a student, I knew I wanted to fight for justice and make
a difference. I’m the daughter of two special education teachers. I was
raised in a working class family that instilled in me the values of hard
work, opportunity, and serving others.

It’s why I started my career investigating threats to democracy and civil
rights in the US and abroad.

It’s why I became a law clerk in Detroit, fighting to protect and defend
people’s civil rights and freedoms.

It’s why, as Dean of Wayne State University Law School, I worked to ensure
all students could afford their education, froze tuition, and expanded
scholarships.

And it’s why, as Secretary of State, I’ve fought to make everyday life
easier for all Michiganders, secure our elections, and expand voter
access.

But I know our work is far from finished. So now, I’m running for Governor
to make sure Michigan is a place where everyone – from our kids to our
seniors – can stay and thrive.

I know that government works best when it’s there when you need it, and
gets out of the way when you don’t. So here’s my promise to you: when we
win this election, I will use every tool available to make life easier:
expand rural healthcare options, build more housing, take on the utility
companies who raise our rates, make childcare free, and ensure anyone can
afford to live in the best place to call home.

But here’s the truth: Michigan is one of the most competitive states in
the entire country, and my opponent has the backing of big billionaires
and special interests. I can only win this race with your support, so
today, I’m asking:

clean_body: Fellow American, I'll keep this message short and sweet. I've got to get back to work; it's a madhouse over here at the GOP. In just a few hours , we are finalizing our checklist before the midterm elections. Unfortunately, according to the report I just read, your name is still missing. I don't know if this is from a technical error or something else, but I was shocked. I've been following your supporter profile for quite a while, and you've always been there when it mattered. Maybe you've been taking a break from the internet, or maybe big tech has been blocking our messages recently. Whatever the case, I wanted to personally check in with you one last time before the midterm elections. If you're willing and able, please confirm you are still standing with us, and you'll be there for us in November! Thank you, and it's been a pleasure working with you these past few months. Mike (GOP H.Q.) Paid for by the Republican National Committee Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee.

body:
Missouri voters were never asked about or consented to these Data Centers

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/z39YcRO_Arp?e=519ef02502&c2id=654d9c3339d5694b9267d382db7ced0e)
| | | | | |

Friend,Across Missouri's 3rd District, I've been meeting with residents who are watching enormous data center developments move toward their communities, often without meaningful public input about what those facilities will mean for their land, water, utility bills, and quality of life.
I've spoken with farmers who are worried about protecting their land, families concerned about rising energy costs, and longtime residents who are frustrated that decisions affecting their communities seem to be happening behind closed doors.
Their concerns deserve more than a public hearing after the important decisions have already been made.
That's why I've called for a **moratorium on new data center construction until Missouri establishes meaningful protections for the communities expected to live alongside these facilities.**
My opponent, Bob Onder, has taken a very different approach. He's publicly championed making Missouri's 3rd District a leader in the data center industry, while I've been standing alongside residents asking a much more important question: **Who actually benefits from these developments, and who gets stuck paying the price?**
I'm not opposed to technological progress or economic development. As a chemist who has spent my career working in agriculture, environmental protection, and critical infrastructure, I understand the importance of innovation. I also understand what happens when we fail to properly account for environmental risks and long-term costs.
That's why my proposal goes beyond simply asking developers to be more transparent. I'm calling for enforceable Community Benefits Agreements negotiated with residents, strong environmental monitoring, protections for private property, prevailing wages and union apprenticeship opportunities, and guarantees that communities share in the financial benefits these facilities generate.
We also need to know what happens when a facility closes, who pays for the cleanup, and whether the people who live nearby will be left dealing with the consequences long after the profits have been collected.
[**[READ MY FULL DATA CENTER PRESS RELEASE →]**](https://us.list-manage.com/RlY9xzWCn4_?e=519ef02502&c2id=654d9c3339d5694b9267d382db7ced0e)
**Here's what I believe:** If a corporation wants to build something that will fundamentally change a community, the people who live there deserve the information, the negotiating power, and the final say.
That shouldn't be controversial, regardless of whether you're a Democrat, Republican, or independent.
The people I've met throughout this district aren't asking for special treatment. They're asking their government to protect their homes, their livelihoods, and their right to make decisions about the places they've spent their lives building.
I believe that's exactly what our elected representatives are supposed to do.
Bob Onder can keep making the case for corporate development. **I'll keep making the case for the people who actually live here.**
Thank you for standing with me and with the Missouri communities fighting to have their voices heard.
Bethany MannCandidate for Congress, Missouri's 3rd District
**P.S. If a data center is being proposed in your community, or you know someone concerned about one, please share my press release with them.** The more Missourians understand what's at stake, the harder it becomes to make these decisions without us.

clean_body: Missouri voters were never asked about or consented to these Data Centers | | | | | | | | | | | Friend,Across Missouri's 3rd District, I've been meeting with residents who are watching enormous data center developments move toward their communities, often without meaningful public input about what those facilities will mean for their land, water, utility bills, and quality of life. I've spoken with farmers who are worried about protecting their land, families concerned about rising energy costs, and longtime residents who are frustrated that decisions affecting their communities seem to be happening behind closed doors. Their concerns deserve more than a public hearing after the important decisions have already been made. That's why I've called for a moratorium on new data center construction until Missouri establishes meaningful protections for the communities expected to live alongside these facilities. My opponent, Bob Onder, has taken a very different approach. He's publicly championed making Missouri's 3rd District a leader in the data center industry, while I've been standing alongside residents asking a much more important question: Who actually benefits from these developments, and who gets stuck paying the price? I'm not opposed to technological progress or economic development. As a chemist who has spent my career working in agriculture, environmental protection, and critical infrastructure, I understand the importance of innovation. I also understand what happens when we fail to properly account for environmental risks and long-term costs. That's why my proposal goes beyond simply asking developers to be more transparent. I'm calling for enforceable Community Benefits Agreements negotiated with residents, strong environmental monitoring, protections for private property, prevailing wages and union apprenticeship opportunities, and guarantees that communities share in the financial benefits these facilities generate. We also need to know what happens when a facility closes, who pays for the cleanup, and whether the people who live nearby will be left dealing with the consequences long after the profits have been collected. [[READ MY FULL DATA CENTER PRESS RELEASE →]]() Here's what I believe: If a corporation wants to build something that will fundamentally change a community, the people who live there deserve the information, the negotiating power, and the final say. That shouldn't be controversial, regardless of whether you're a Democrat, Republican, or independent. The people I've met throughout this district aren't asking for special treatment. They're asking their government to protect their homes, their livelihoods, and their right to make decisions about the places they've spent their lives building. I believe that's exactly what our elected representatives are supposed to do. Bob Onder can keep making the case for corporate development. I'll keep making the case for the people who actually live here. Thank you for standing with me and with the Missouri communities fighting to have their voices heard. Bethany MannCandidate for Congress, Missouri's 3rd District P.S. If a data center is being proposed in your community, or you know someone concerned about one, please share my press release with them. The more Missourians understand what's at stake, the harder it becomes to make these decisions without us. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Bethany Mann for Congress PO Box 12 Wentzville, MO 63385 * USA or |

---
I’ll explain why in a second. [**_But if that’s all you need to hear, please split a donation between my campaign and Anita’s today._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19865?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1706&amount=5&t=8&akid=4379%2E124072%2EPfjmLn)

---
Back in 2024, North Carolinians elected Justice Allison Riggs to the NC Supreme Court by the slimmest of margins: **734 votes out of 5.5 million cast.** Her election took nearly six months and was the last race in the nation to be certified.
But that isn’t because of the margin, at least not entirely. It’s because her opponent and state Republicans asked the courts to throw out 60,000 legal ballots after the election. **In effect, they tried to change the rules after the game was already played.**
That meant that some North Carolinians registered to vote before the state changed our voter registration requirements; some cast their ballots from overseas; and active-duty military North Carolinians mailed their ballots from wherever they were stationed at the time.
All of these were legal ballots, and state Republicans tried to throw them out anyway. **Those are the lengths they were willing to go to flip a seat on our Supreme Court in 2024 and we must anticipate that it will be no different this time around.**
Justice Anita Earls stands for accountability, keeping our communities safe and equal justice for all under the law. It’s imperative we re-elect her.
[**_I hope you’re with me. If you are, please chip in a donation between my campaign and hers today._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/19865?refcode=email_bu_pros_jtk1706&amount=5&t=10&akid=4379%2E124072%2EPfjmLn)
Thank you, Peter.

Roy Cooper

name: Wes Moore
subject: Conversation
body:
What I said on Jubilee.
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2094%2E1086043%2EgaVQgb)
A few weeks ago, I sat down for Jubilee’s _Surrounded_ and debated with 20 people who had not voted in the last election.
**The cynics out there in the world tell us a conversation like the one I had isn’t worth having.** That we’ve become too divided. That everyone has already chosen a side, and the only thing left to do is shout louder than our political opponents.
But that isn’t what I saw in that room. And I do not think it is true in this country. We haven’t crossed a threshold where we can no longer listen to one another or to work together.
The year that we celebrated America’s 250th anniversary, I’m struck by the fact that our nation’s story has never been one of perfection. It’s one of progress. Generation after generation, Americans have chosen to do their part in expanding the promise of this country.
That work has never been automatic. It has always required participation from people who believe that tomorrow can be better than today.
**[If you share that belief with me, I would appreciate a donation to our re-election campaign today so we can continue our work.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261010-3.SJvvBI&refcode=em-20261010-3&t=2&akid=2094%2E1086043%2EgaVQgb)**
I did not go into _Surrounded_ – or write this – to shame people who have opted out of the system.
Quite the contrary. I understand that choice.
I don’t come from a political background. When I ran for office the first time a few years ago, I had to convince many of my family members to vote for me. It’s not like we aren’t cool. They just don’t rush to the ballot box every year.
It struck me that people I love – people who cared deeply about their communities and their country – had been absent from a democratic act that generations of Americans fought for.
Somewhere along the way, they stopped believing that politics had much to do with them – or that anyone in politics had much interest in them. That realization has stayed with me. And it is exactly why I did _Surrounded._
Democracy is a relationship. Those who have the privilege of serving in government share a responsibility to give people a reason to believe their participation counts. To earn their trust. To show the public that government is not something that happens to us, but something we have the power to shape. As an elected official, I take that responsibility seriously. It’s sacred, and essential.
If those of us in public office do our jobs right, then voting becomes about more than casting a ballot. It is an act of hope.
If we’re serious about strengthening democracy over the next 250 years, we cannot only invest in elections. _We have to invest in one another._ The work of patriotism is not passive, and it is not performative. It is service.
Real patriotism asks us to see our humanity in each other before we see our differences. It asks us to remember that the future of this country has always depended on ordinary people doing extraordinary things together – not because they agreed on everything, but because they believed this nation was worth building together, despite our disagreements.
**[If you’re with me, and you believe in what we’re building together, can you chip in any amount to our campaign today?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261010-3.SJvvBI&refcode=em-20261010-3&t=3&akid=2094%2E1086043%2EgaVQgb)**
My final challenge is a simple one: Sit down with people in your life and in your community who disagree with you. Have honest conversations. Listen. You may be surprised by what you find. And you may even end up working together to make a big difference in our world.
Elevate,
Wes

The year that we celebrated America’s 250th anniversary, I’m struck by the fact that our nation’s story has never been one of perfection. It’s one of progress. Generation after generation, Americans have chosen to do their part in expanding the promise of this country. That work has never been automatic. It has always required participation from people who believe that tomorrow can be better than today. I did not go into Surrounded – or write this – to shame people who have opted out of the system. Quite the contrary. I understand that choice. I don’t come from a political background. When I ran for office the first time a few years ago, I had to convince many of my family members to vote for me. It’s not like we aren’t cool. They just don’t rush to the ballot box every year. It struck me that people I love – people who cared deeply about their communities and their country – had been absent from a democratic act that generations of Americans fought for. Somewhere along the way, they stopped believing that politics had much to do with them – or that anyone in politics had much interest in them. That realization has stayed with me. And it is exactly why I did Surrounded. Democracy is a relationship. Those who have the privilege of serving in government share a responsibility to give people a reason to believe their participation counts. To earn their trust. To show the public that government is not something that happens to us, but something we have the power to shape. As an elected official, I take that responsibility seriously. It’s sacred, and essential. If those of us in public office do our jobs right, then voting becomes about more than casting a ballot. It is an act of hope. If we’re serious about strengthening democracy over the next 250 years, we cannot only invest in elections. We have to invest in one another. The work of patriotism is not passive, and it is not performative. It is service. Real patriotism asks us to see our humanity in each other before we see our differences. It asks us to remember that the future of this country has always depended on ordinary people doing extraordinary things together – not because they agreed on everything, but because they believed this nation was worth building together, despite our disagreements. My final challenge is a simple one: Sit down with people in your life and in your community who disagree with you. Have honest conversations. Listen. You may be surprised by what you find. And you may even end up working together to make a big difference in our world. Elevate, Wes

Friend 🐾,

I’m barking in your inbox today because I’ve been one busy pup! My mom brought me along to a very special place: **Chaco Canyon!**
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1541-fr-nd&t=2&akid=13038%2E400544%2Ebb1-n-)
I got to explore, take in all the new smells, and spend some time outside with my mom. But I know Chaco isn’t just a great place for a walk. It’s a sacred place that means so much to my mom, Tribal communities, and generations of New Mexicans.
**Chaco holds a special place in my mom’s heart. She’s spent years fighting to protect it and the other sacred lands that make New Mexico so special. And as Governor, she’ll keep fighting to make sure these places are here for generations to come._But she can’t do it alone_. ****[Will you paw-lease chip in $5 or $10 today to give my mom the resources she needs to win this election and keep protecting New Mexico?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17387?refcode=jtk1541-fr-nd&t=3&akid=13038%2E400544%2Ebb1-n-)**

I may be just a pup, but even I know there’s something special about this place. I watched my mom take it all in, and I could tell Chaco means more to her than just a beautiful place to visit.
It reminded her of all the time she spent outside with her dad. She grew up running through the desert with her cousins and fishing with him. Those memories taught her that we have a responsibility to take care of the places we call home.

_And that’s why she’s so worried about what’s happening right now._
Donald Trump is moving to slash protections for the lands surrounding Chaco and reopen them to mining and oil and gas drilling. **That means putting a place that has been sacred to Indigenous peoples since time immemorial at risk.**

**My mom says Chaco is not for sale.**

It’s amazing that your response can make that kind of difference for

Supported by you, BRAVE for Good gives parents the tools they need to
rebuild our families and reclaim America with the Biblical values our
country was founded upon.

Now I know there are a lot of places you can spend your money in the
next ten minutes.

BUT I HOPE YOU’LL BE A PART OF HISTORY BY SUPPORTING IGGY AND MR.
KIRK.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Hollywood groomers have destroyed America’s Godly culture. But today
we rebuild from the ashes.

And it starts by ensuring the most innocent among us are filled with
faith and family – not filth.

Thank you for joining us in the fight.

Sincerely,

DR. TRENT TALBOT

subject: THIS MONDAY: Virtual Phone Bank with Congressman Derek Tran & Marni von Wilpert
body:
You’re invited to Monday’s Take Back The House virtual phone bank with Congressman Derek Tran and Red-to-Blue candidate for CA-48 Marni von

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/derektranforcongress/2026-oct-12-phone-bank-blast?e=fa48019594)
---
| | | | |
---
| | Dear Supporter,
You’re invited to Monday’s _**Take Back The House**_ virtual phone bank with Congressman Derek Tran and Red-to-Blue candidate for CA-48 Marni von Wilpert!
**WHEN:** Monday, October 12 5 - 7 p.m. PST**WHERE:** Virtual**RSVP:**[**HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/PwStXW1cdJu?e=fa48019594&c2id=2d2f4814b3c86de5c7569386ec1a86b4)
To receive your virtual meeting link, phone bank training, and hear from Marni on our plan to take back the House, please RSVP via the link above. I hope to see you there!
Sincerely,Congressman Derek Tran
---
| | ###
_The son of refugees who worked hard and sacrificed for the American Dream, Congressman Derek Tran joined the Army at 18 to give back to the country that has given him so much. Wanting to continue his career in public service, he ran in California's 45th district to put people ahead of politics and protect democracy, and won. Now, he's running again to ensure everyone no matter what neighborhood they come from has the opportunity to succeed without fear of their freedoms being taken away._
_California’s 45th Congressional District remains one of the most contested battleground races in the country. Last cycle, Derek Tran flipped the seat by just over 600 votes (a 0.2% margin) in the second-closest and most expensive House race ($46 million spent) in the country. A majority-minority district, the District has the third largest AAPI population (41%) of any Congressional District, is 28% Latino, and is home to the largest Vietnamese community in the country. Following Proposition 50, this district brings in over 15,000 new Hispanic voters and over 7,000 new Vietnamese voters, and has a DPI of 52.8%. It includes all or part of the cities of Garden Grove, Westminster, Fountain Valley, Cerritos, Buena Park, Placentia, Hawaiian Gardens, Cypress, Artesia, Los Alamitos, La Palma, Norwalk, Stanton, Lakewood, Santa Ana, Seal Beach, and Fullerton, as well as the unincorporated community of Midway City._
_Use of Derek Tran's military rank, job titles, and photographs in uniform does not imply endorsement by the Dept. of Defense or U.S. Army._

On September 4, 2026, Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial in Plymouth Superior Court, ending five weeks of testimony in the case of Lindsay Clancy -- the Duxbury mother who never denied killing her three children, Callan, Dawson, and Cora, ages eight months to five years. The jury had told the court, in a note her lawyer characterized, that it was split 11-1, with eleven leaning toward not guilty by reason of insanity. One holdout, a juror who later told reporters he saw no evidence justifying his vote, was all that stood between Clancy and a hospital instead of a prison. On October 2, the judge denied the defense's request to simply find her not guilty after the mistrial. A retrial now looms.
Then the headlines kept coming.
Since the mistrial -- and through the 2020s running -- the maternal-filicide file has grown thick:...

Every day, Washington politicians try to push America into a socialist future –** It’s time to settle the score. We launched the official Capitalist vs. Socialist Belief Survey to determine which worldview drives the America First movement. Are you a die-hard**CAPITALISTor a big-governmentSOCIALIST? | CAPITALIST VS SOCIALIST BELIEF SURVEY Select which view best aligns with your own on key topics. Due by 11:59 PM TONIGHT. HEALTH CARE [[ ] OPTION A:]() Government-run healthcare with higher taxes, long wait times, and political control over your medical decisions. [[ ] OPTION B:]() Quality private healthcare that gives you freedom of choice, personalized care, and affordable coverage options. [[ ] OPTION B:]() Low taxes that let you keep more of your hard-earned money and encourage business growth and job creation. BORDER SECURITY & ICE [[ ] OPTION A:]() Weakening border enforcement, dismantling ICE, and letting open-border policies compromise public safety. [[ ] OPTION B:]() Strong border security and a fully funded ICE to protect our communities, uphold the law, and keep neighborhoods safe. HOUSING [[ ] OPTION A:]() Heavy government housing regulations that cause shortages, drive up costs, and hurt property values. [[ ] OPTION B:]() Free-market housing that builds more affordable homes, protects property rights, and expands homeownership. ENERGY AND JOBS [[ ] OPTION A:]() Costly government energy mandates that destroy traditional jobs, raise electric bills, and hurt working families. [[ ] OPTION B:]() Reliable American energy production that keeps fuel prices low, creates well-paying jobs, and keeps our economy strong. FREE SPEECH [[ ] OPTION A:]() Heavy state regulation of social media and online platforms to censor "misinformation," control public narratives, and penalize hate speech. [[ ] OPTION B:]() Protecting free speech online, allowing private platforms to compete freely, and letting users choose which platforms and content they consume. [[ ] OPTION B:]() Protecting constitutional gun rights, allowing citizens to defend themselves, and preserving private firearm ownership without federal interference. name: Governor Phil Scott
subject: Economic Growth Must Be Our Priority
body:
Economic Growth Must Be Our Priority |
---
| |
---
| **Economic Growth Must Be a Priority**
Dear Friends -

_**In order to make Vermont more affordable we must grow our economy**_.

My team has gained ground in this area (without a lot of support from the legislature), the job is far from over, but the roadmap is clear:

We must build more housing, cut the red tape, stop trying to solve every problem by raising taxes and fees; reform education and health care to lower costs; invest in infrastructure and downtowns across the state; and strengthen our workforce.

**These aren’t radical ideas. This is a commonsense approach that’s been proven time and time again.**

Growth in the economy improves the everyday lives of Vermonters. That’s why it’s been my focus for my many years of public service.

**Today, that basic principle is being challenged**.

When asked whether Vermont should move _away_ from economic growth as a priority, my opponent responded:

[“Yeah, I mean, honestly, I don't think it's that hard because everybody's struggling so much economically.”](https://us.list-manage.com/FkKgovW1tyP?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c)

**_Now... I’m NOT an economist, but my 35 years in business has taught me that when an economy stops growing— or shrinks — it’s called a recession..._

That hurts working families the hardest: jobs become less secure, household incomes stagnate or fall, tax burdens sometimes increase, public services come under pressure, and young families leave in search of opportunity elsewhere.**

Abandoning our work to grow the economy is not the answer... because a healthy economy lifts all boats.

So... I need your help and your vote. To finish the job we started—to grow the economy, attract more business, help the businesses who are here be able to stay; build more housing, get a handle on property taxes and health care costs, and become a more affordable place to live, work and raise a family.

**But I can’t do it alone, which is why my team and I are asking for your support over the next 28 days. You can reach out to us at[www.philscott.org](https://us.list-manage.com/wXI6lifgrbF?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c) to request a lawn sign or volunteer and you can make a contribution by clicking the link below.**

Sincerely,

Governor Scott

Peter, As I’ve spoken with people across the country, I’m often asked: What does the Democratic Party stand for? I’m a New Deal Democrat. So for me, the answer is simple. I believe our party should put workers and families at the heart of every policy. But for years, the answer to the question “what do democrats stand for” has been to point to the other side, saying: “reverse what Trump did” or “at least we’re not them.” **That tells people who we oppose. It doesn’t tell them what we stand for.**

FDR’s New Deal showed that government could lift people out of hardship and help them live with dignity. We need that ambition again. I’m a New Deal Democrat. So for me, the answer is simple. I believe our party should put workers and families at the heart of every policy.
